note:
A static, curated dataset of Ethereum-ecosystem funding opportunities, maintained in this repository and versioned with it. Every document validates against RFP Hub Standard v1.0.0 with zero errors.

PROVENANCE, IN TWO CLASSES, TOLD BY THE ID NAMESPACE. `fundingmap:` records were converted from a snapshot of an upstream registry and then reconciled against the funder's own published pages; they keep the identifier that registry issued in `source.originalId`. `curated:` records were researched here from the funder's own pages — site, docs, blog, governance forum or code host — and never existed in any upstream registry, so they carry no `source.originalId` and no upstream namespace. `source.ingestedVia` is `import` on both classes because both entered the Hub through a seed import; it describes the route in, not an upstream API. Where a researched value contradicted a converted one, the researched value was kept.

WHAT THE PROVENANCE FIELDS DO AND DO NOT SAY. `source.verifiedAgainstSource` is null on every document: it records the verification-assist job, which has not run, not the human curation pass, which has. The reconciliation is evidenced by `additionalReferences` and by the dated readings in the descriptions, not by a machine-readable flag.

DATES. `postedAt` is the date the source itself announced the opportunity — a program page's "Live Since" line, a governance topic's creation date, a launch post or press release — and is never the date this file was edited. Seven records carry an archival bound instead ("publicly visible by", the first capture of the funder's own page), because their funder published no announcement at all; each of those says so in its own description. `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are Hub timestamps — for `curated:` records that is the curation date, which is what those fields mean.

CAVEATS. Statuses are a point-in-time reading as of 2026-08-11 and go stale: re-check against the funder before relying on one. Descriptions summarise and often quote the funder's own copy, promotional register included; they are reporting, not endorsement.

documents.title: Optimism Season 9 — Audit Grants
documents.description:
**Discontinued.** Audit Grants were the Developer Advisory Board's (DAB) grant track under the Optimism Collective's Governance Fund. The DAB subsidised third-party smart-contract security audits for teams building on the Superchain; projects did not apply directly but worked with whitelisted Audit Service Providers (ASPs), who applied for the grant on the project's behalf.

**Season 9 window.** Season 9 ran from 29 January 2026 to 3 June 2026. The Grants Council closed Season 9 submissions on 20 May 2026.

**Budget.** The Developer Advisory Board's Season 9 Governance Fund mission budget was 0.98M OP (up from 949k OP in Season 8). That single budget line covered both Audit Grants and Foundation Missions — Optimism did not publish an audit-only sub-budget for Season 9.

**Process.** Audit Grant applications were reviewed on a rolling basis inside the season by the DAB's Audit Program Stewards, with a target of an initial response to every applicant within 14 days (max) of submission. Steward funding recommendations were optimistically approved by the seven voting Board members; results were published as per-cycle reports on gov.optimism.io.

**Why it is closed.** The Guide to Season 9 announced the Foundation's intent to wind down community-led capital allocation. Governance Update #12 (3 June 2026) confirmed there would be no dedicated Seasons after Season 9. On 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Foundation's Developer Advisory Board Dissolution Proposal (22.33M OP For / 198.45K Against), dissolving the board that ran this program, effective immediately. The former intake site opgrants.io no longer completes a TLS handshake and no replacement audit-grant intake has been published.
documents.summary: Optimism's Season 9 Audit Grants subsidised security audits for Superchain builders via whitelisted Audit Service Providers, run by the Developer Advisory Board out of a 0.98M OP Governance Fund mission budget. Submissions closed 20 May 2026; the Board was dissolved by Token House vote on 15 July 2026 and the program is discontinued.

documents.title: Optimism Season 9 — Growth Grants
documents.description:
**Discontinued.** Growth Grants were the Grants Council's proactive incentive-grant track under the Optimism Collective's Season 9 Governance Fund mission.

**Mission scope.** The Season 9 primary success metric was *DEX TVL for collateral-borrow pairs that exist on lending markets* (e.g. Morpho, Aave) — both assets in a liquidity pair had to be available on a lending market (e.g. a WETH/USDC DEX pool where WETH is collateral and USDC is the borrowed asset). The secondary metric was DEX trading volume per TVL for those same pairs. Impact was measured at the end of the Season by OP Labs or Open Source Observer.

**Window.** Season 9 ran 29 January 2026 to 3 June 2026; the Grants Council closed Season 9 submissions on 20 May 2026.

**Budget and outcome.** The Season 9 Grants Council budget was 3,690,000 OP (the Budget Board's proposed mission figure was 3.89M OP, down from ~6.29M OP in Season 8); 90,000 OP was returned unallocated at the end of the season. Season 9 drew 38 applications in total. Applications first passed an AI filter, then GrantNerds human review, then the Grants Council; GrantNerds reviewed 29 applications and passed 10 to the Council, of which 4 were funded, while the Council reviewed a further 19 directly and passed 8. Approved Season 9 growth grants in the final cycle ranged from 150,000 OP to 1,000,000 OP.

**Where it was submitted, and why no `applicationUrl` is recorded.** Optimism published the Season 9 intake as a Growth Grant form on its own grants platform, linked from its season page directly above "Applications Open: Feb 11th 2026 / Submissions Closes: May 20th 2026", and the season's own reports link individual submissions there. That host no longer completes a TLS handshake — there is no HTTP status at all, not even an error — and only archive captures of the form remain. An archived copy of a form is not a place to apply, so the field is left absent.

**Why it is closed.** Governance Update #12 (3 June 2026) confirmed there would be no dedicated Seasons after Season 9. On 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Foundation's Grants Council Dissolution Proposal (22.34M OP For / 196.6K Against), effective immediately. The Foundation stated it will continue to make select strategic grants directly in pursuit of the OP Enterprise strategy, but community-led capital allocation has ended.
documents.summary: Optimism's Season 9 Growth Grants funded OP incentives to deepen DEX liquidity for collateral-borrow asset pairs used on lending markets, from a 3,690,000 OP Grants Council budget. Submissions closed 20 May 2026 and the Grants Council was dissolved by Token House vote on 15 July 2026; the program is discontinued.

documents.title: Optimism Audit Service Providers (ASP)
documents.description:
**Discontinued.** The Audit Service Provider (ASP) track was the delivery mechanism for Optimism's Audit Grants. Rather than projects applying for audit money and then sourcing an auditor, the Grants Council (and, from Season 8, the Developer Advisory Board) pre-whitelisted audit firms; whitelisted ASPs then applied for specific audits and drew directly against the standing audit budget on the project's behalf. The stated aim of the model was to remove per-auditor pre-approved budgets and treat audits like any other grant in the system.

**Governance and process.** In Seasons 8 and 9 the program sat with the Developer Advisory Board under a non-voting Lead plus seven voting Board Members, with two designated Audit Stewards. Applications were accepted on a rolling basis, with a target initial response to every applicant within 14 days (max) of submission; Steward funding recommendations were optimistically approved by the Board, and results were published as per-cycle reports on gov.optimism.io. Members had to declare conflicts of interest (employment, investment, advisory roles, code contributions) with respect to applicants.

**Budget, and the season it belongs to.** Every Season 8 audit cycle report restates the same line — "Season 8 Audit Grants Budget: 581,726.40 OP" — and the last of them, Cycle 45, closes with "Remaining Budget: 8,798.40 OP". So 572,928 OP of that pool was allocated over the season, which the per-cycle approvals confirm exactly: 123,300 + 110,750 + 0 + 111,800 + 227,078. Both figures are **Season 8 only**. They are the audit-only slice carved out of that season's 949k OP Developer Advisory Board mission line, and they are not the sibling Season 9 record's 0.98M OP, which is a combined Audit Grants and Foundation Missions budget. **No Season 9 audit-only budget was ever published** — there is no Season 9 audit cycle report at all, Cycle 45 (December 2025) being the most recent of any season — so nothing here is carried into that season.

**Scale.** Approved audit grants in the Season 8 cycles (41-45) ran from 18,500 OP to 90,300 OP per project. Optimism did not publish a per-audit cap.

**Where it was submitted, and why no `applicationUrl` is recorded.** Optimism's own grants-site navigation separated "Audit Grants", which pointed at its mission page, from "Audit Service Provider", which pointed at this program's page on its grants platform — that program page was the ASP entry point. The form behind it was never archived, and the host answers nothing today, so there is neither a live URL nor a captured form to record and the field is left absent.

**Why it is closed.** Governance Update #12 (3 June 2026) confirmed no dedicated Seasons after Season 9, and on 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Developer Advisory Board Dissolution Proposal (22.33M OP For / 198.45K Against), dissolving the board that ran the ASP whitelist and the Audit Grants program, effective immediately. The intake site opgrants.io no longer completes a TLS handshake, and no replacement ASP whitelist or audit-grant intake has been published on optimism.io, docs.optimism.io or gov.optimism.io.
documents.summary: Optimism's Audit Service Provider model let pre-whitelisted audit firms apply for Superchain audit subsidies on a project's behalf, run in Seasons 8-9 by the Developer Advisory Board on a rolling basis with a 14-day initial-response target. The Board was dissolved by Token House vote on 15 July 2026 and the intake site opgrants.io is unreachable; the program is discontinued.

documents.title: Build Agents for the Real World Hackathon V2
documents.description:
Build Agents for the Real World — Celo Hackathon V2 challenged teams to build agentic applications on Celo, an Ethereum Layer 2 designed for fast, low-cost global payments. The hackathon ran 2 March 2026 (kick-off, 5 PM GMT) to 23 March 2026 (submissions close, 9 AM GMT), with winners announced 24 March 2026 at 3 PM GMT. It carried an 8,500 USD₮ (USDT) prize pool, sponsored by CeloPG.

**Prize distribution**

- Track 1 — Best Agent on Celo: 1st 3,000 USD₮, 2nd 2,000 USD₮, 3rd 1,000 USD₮
- Track 2 — Best Agent Infra on Celo: 1st 2,000 USD₮
- Track 3 — Highest Rank in 8004scan for Celo (combinable with the other tracks): 1st 500 USD₮

**How to participate**

Register the project with a website link, demo video link, GitHub repository link(s), pitch deck link and contact info; join the Telegram group for support and announcements; tweet about the agent linking the project, the agentscan Registry agentId (not required for the Infra track) and optionally Self AI and a Molthunt registration, tagging @Celo, @CeloDevs and @CeloPG; then submit the tweet and project link through the hackathon form.

All agent frameworks were allowed — the frameworks named in the idea list were suggestions only. Judges were Luuk (CeloPG), Viral Sangani (AI Lead, Celo) and Marek (CEO, Celo). Community partners were ETH Nigeria and ETH Lagos.
documents.summary: Build your agent for the real world on Celo: an Agentic hackathon with a $8.5k USD₮ prize pool.

documents.title: Polygon Prediction Markets Program
documents.description:
**Intake retired.** The Polygon Prediction Markets Program was an intake path connecting prediction-market builders (including teams integrating with Polymarket) to Polygon funding, technical guidance and potential BD partnerships. It was operated by Polygon Labs.

**Current state as of 11 August 2026.** The program's intake domain, founders.polygon.technology, no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN), and its stated window closed on 16 February 2026. Polygon Labs' own site no longer carries a founder-funding or grants section: polygon.technology/grants, polygon.technology/grow and polygon.technology/village all return HTTP 301 redirects to https://hadronfc.com, the Hadron Founders Club — a community/accelerator programme offering global events, founder bootcamps, mentorship, fundraising support and IRL campuses in Dubai and New York (the NYC space is described as being for 'hadron founders & polygon builders'), with intake via an Airtable application form. polygon.technology/founders and polygon.technology/build return 404. Polygon Labs' current publishing (blog through August 2026) is focused entirely on payments, stablecoins and enterprise infrastructure, with no prediction-markets funding call.

No prediction-markets-specific replacement intake could be verified on any live Polygon Labs page.

**No figure was ever published, and no form survives.** Polygon left every money field on this program's own record at zero — no budget, no minimum or maximum grant size, nothing distributed — and the program text promises funding only in general terms: "This intake form connects qualified projects with Polygon funding and technical resources" and "We support the next generation of prediction market builders through grants, technical guidance, and potential BD partnerships." The program page's details panel carries nothing but the closing date. The nearest figure anywhere is the Community Treasury Board's ecosystem-wide season cap — "the CTB intends to allocate a maximum budget of 80 million POL" — which covers a whole treasury season rather than this program and is deliberately not recorded here.

The intake itself cannot be pointed at honestly either. The funder-branded form URL was never archived, and the only live rendering of the same intake sits on another ecosystem's branded instance of the platform Polygon ran it on — correct, but misleading on a Polygon opportunity — so this record carries no `applicationUrl`.
documents.summary: Polygon Labs' prediction-markets intake is retired: the founders.polygon.technology intake domain no longer resolves, the stated window closed 16 February 2026, and polygon.technology's founder and grants paths now redirect to the Hadron Founders Club. No prediction-markets-specific replacement intake is published.

documents.title: Polygon Audit Support Program
documents.description:
**Closed intake, open marketplace.** The Polygon Audit Support Program was delivered through the Polygon Security Marketplace, built and run by Areta on Polygon Labs' behalf. The funded intake closed on **16 February 2026** — the same cut-off Polygon set for its two other programs of that cycle — and the program page reports that deadline as passed, which is why this record is `closed`. The marketplace itself is unaffected and remains live and free to use, so the accurate reading is a closed funding intake behind an open marketplace rather than a dead page.

**How it works.** Builders submit an audit scope, are matched against a whitelisted auditor pool and receive competing quotes, free of charge. Submit your audit scope through the guided intake flow → explore the verified auditor list → receive roughly 10-12 competing quotes → choose your preferred auditor at transparent pricing → receive the audit under standardised terms. Areta advertises competing quotes within 48 hours.

**Whitelisted providers.** The published Polygon marketplace provider list (20+ vetted auditors) includes ABDK Consulting, Ackee, Adevar Labs, Bailsec, Beosin, 33audits, Cantina/Spearbit Labs, Certora, ChainSecurity, Code4rena, Composable Security, Cyfrin, Dedaub, FYEO, Fuzzland, Guardian, Hacken, Halborn, Hexens, Immunefi, Josselin Feist, Kauz Security Services GmbH, Least Authority, MixBytes, Nethermind, Oak Security, Olympix, Quantstamp, QuillAudits, Runtime Verification, Serokell, Sherlock, Statemind, Veridise, Vidma and Zellic.

**What Polygon published about the money, and what it did not.** The published rule is qualitative and carries no number: "Partial or full reimbursement of audit costs (depending on project scope)". Beyond it, every money field on the program's own record is zero, and no pool, no subsidy percentage and no per-project cap appears on any Polygon or Areta page. The contrast on the marketplace's own FAQ is decisive: the Polygon section has no subsidy entry at all, while the same file's 0G section reads "capped at 30% of the quote price" and its Uniswap section advertises subsidies "of up to 100%". The "up to 50% savings on audit costs" the marketplace markets is a competitive-quoting claim, not a Polygon-funded subsidy — and the intake's own first step asks builders to confirm "I have applied/will apply for a grant via Polygon Foundation for this audit request", which is where the money actually comes from. So this record carries no `fundingInfo`: the reimbursement rule is real and is quoted above, and it has no figure in it.
documents.summary: Polygon's audit support ran through the Areta-operated Polygon Security Marketplace: free for builders, submit an audit scope and get competing quotes from 20+ whitelisted auditors within 48 hours. The funded intake closed on 16 February 2026 while the marketplace stayed live and free. Polygon published a qualitative reimbursement rule — partial or full, depending on scope — and never a percentage, a pool or a per-project cap.

documents.title: Polygon Growth Partnership Program
documents.description:
**Intake retired. Not a grant program.** Polygon /grow connected payments-focused projects to Polygon Labs' business-development and founder-support teams for strategic partnerships, integrations and ecosystem growth — explicitly not a funding program.

**Current state as of 11 August 2026.** Its stated window closed on 16 February 2026, and the /grow path itself no longer serves the program: https://polygon.technology/grow now returns an HTTP 301 redirect to https://hadronfc.com, the Hadron Founders Club (the same target as polygon.technology/grants and polygon.technology/village). Hadron describes itself as an exclusive community of founders, builders and creators offering global events, founder bootcamps, mentorship, closed-door speaker sessions, fundraising support and IRL campuses in Dubai and New York — the NYC space is described as being 'for hadron founders & polygon builders'. Intake is via an Airtable application form linked from hadronfc.com. polygon.technology/founders and polygon.technology/build return 404.

**The intake URL, and what is left of it.** Polygon published the form as founders.polygon.technology/programs/981/apply and linked it from polygon.technology/grow ("Join the Polygon Founders Community Telegram and submit an application to S3"). The form itself is archived — "Apply for Polygon Growth Partnership Program", asking for team and contact details, project description, project vertical, stage of development and current traction — but the host is gone: founders.polygon.technology has no DNS record at all. The URL is on this record because it is the address the funder published for this closed program, not because anything answers on it.

This is the closest live successor to Polygon's founder/partnership intake, but it is a founders' club rather than the /grow BD-partnership funnel described in this record.

**No figure, and none was ever intended.** Polygon says so in the program text — "This is not a grant program - it's designed to identify established projects for deeper business relationships, technical partnerships, and ecosystem integration opportunities" — and the apply page repeats it more bluntly still: "This is not a grants program, and we are not issuing upfront grant funding through this application." Every money field on the program's own record is zero. The figures that sit on polygon.technology/grow — $1B POL over ten years, 80M POL available through 2025, a grants tracker reading 17M POL deployed across 114 approved grants — belong to the Polygon Community Treasury and its grants seasons, not to this program, and are deliberately not recorded here.
documents.summary: Polygon /grow was a business-development and partnership funnel for payments-focused projects, not a grant program. Its window closed 16 February 2026 and polygon.technology/grow now redirects to the Hadron Founders Club (hadronfc.com), whose Airtable form is the closest live successor intake.

The intake itself was not payments-only: its project-vertical list read Payments, Tokenization, DeFi, Prediction Markets, Other. Hadron Founders Club, the current live successor intake, publishes no equivalent eligibility criteria beyond being a founder, builder or creator.

documents.title: GEN Ukraine MicroGrant Program
documents.description:
The GEN Grant Program 01 enables a bioregional network of ecovillages to implement regenerative projects through Ethereum-aligned coordination and transparent on-chain micro-funding. Leveraging DAO governance, ReFi tools, and on-chain verification, the program funds solar resilience, water restoration, biodiversity monitoring, and community infrastructure to strengthen local regenerative capacity and decentralized economic resilience.

**Currency.** The 5,000 figure on this record reaches the corpus without a unit, and the unit is USD. The program states its own co-funding as "Confirmed co-funding of $5,000 is already secured through two on-chain community pools" and sizes the round it belongs to in dollars throughout — "We aim to raise a total of $20,000 for this round", split "60% - Local Micro-Grants ($12,000) / 20% - Program Operations & Coordination ($4,000)" and so on. Its funder's round rules are dollar-denominated too: a $125,000 USD matching pool with a "Grant Range: $5,000 - $20,000 per local program". The program's implementation report prices every disbursement in dollars as well. USD is recorded as the unit of account; the settlement rails are stablecoins (cUSD, USDC, USDGLO) and are not the denomination.

**Intake ran through the network, not through a form.** The program states that funding "will be distributed through Sarafu Network community pools" with application intake integrated into the coordination workspace GEN Ukraine already used, and its own timeline reads "Announcement & Intake (Jan 2026) - Publicly announce the GEN Ukraine Local Grant Program through our network channels ... Open call for proposals from 20+ ecovillages." Twelve applications were coordinated that way. documents.title: Optimism Season 8 — Audit Grants
documents.description:
**Concluded.** Season 8 Audit Grants subsidised third-party smart-contract security audits for teams building on the Superchain. It was the first season in which audit grants sat with the Developer Advisory Board rather than inside the Grants Council budget. Projects worked with whitelisted Audit Service Providers who applied on their behalf.

**Budget and outcome.** The Season 8 Audit Grants budget was 581,726.40 OP, of which only 8,798.40 OP remained after the season's final cycle (Cycle 45). This budget sat inside the Developer Advisory Board's wider 949k OP Season 8 Governance Fund mission, which also covered Foundation Missions. For context, audit grants in earlier seasons totalled roughly 2.5M OP: 200,000 OP in S4, 665,000 OP in S5, 640,000 OP in S6 and 990,000 OP in S7.

**Cycles.** The season ran across Cycles 41-45. Approved grants per project ranged from 18,500 OP to 90,300 OP (Cycle 41: FinDEX 90,300 OP, SuperDCA 33,000 OP; Cycle 42: Own Protocol 48,250 OP, TrueMarkets 62,500 OP; Cycle 43: none approved; Cycle 44: Highway 52,800 OP, WannaBet 18,500 OP, Predifi 40,500 OP; Cycle 45: Metrom 25,200 OP, 40acres 75,000 OP, VII Finance 72,928 OP, Arcadia Finance 53,950 OP). Demand far exceeded supply — Cycle 45 alone saw 1,711,089.32 OP requested against 227,078 OP approved, and the final rejections were driven primarily by budget exhaustion.

**Successor and end state.** Season 8 rolled into Season 9 (29 January - 3 June 2026), which was Optimism's final grant-making season. The Developer Advisory Board was dissolved by Token House vote on 15 July 2026 and the intake site opgrants.io is unreachable.
documents.summary: Optimism's Season 8 Audit Grants ran across Cycles 41-45 on a 581,726.40 OP budget managed by the Developer Advisory Board, approving individual audit subsidies of 18,500-90,300 OP and exhausting all but 8,798.40 OP. The season is closed; the Board was dissolved by governance vote on 15 July 2026.

documents.title: Optimism Season 8 — Growth Grants
documents.description:
**Concluded.** Season 8 Growth Grants were the Grants Council's proactive incentive-grant track under the Optimism Collective's Season 8 Governance Fund mission.

**Mission scope — a correction.** The mission was narrower than 'increase the TVL of the Superchain'. Season 8's success metrics were specifically (1) *interop-ready TVL* — TVL/AOP that is interop-ready within the Interop set, and its share of total TVL/AOP — and (2) *interop transaction fees*, measured as ETH per month in transaction fees generated by transactions interacting with the L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger contract, and their share versus non-interop fees. The rationale was that growing the volume and share of interop-compatible assets increases the chance interop is widely adopted.

**Budget.** 6.29M OP from the Governance Fund, down from roughly 9M OP in Season 7 (excluding audit grants). Season 9 cut this again to 3.69M OP.

**Process.** The Grants Council set its own selection algorithm, which had to be published as a public rubric on the forum before the first round of selection. Selected projects were assessed against the success metrics by OP Labs or Open Source Observer at the end of the Season.

**Successor and end state.** Season 8 was followed by Season 9 (29 January - 3 June 2026), Optimism's final grant-making season. On 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Grants Council Dissolution Proposal (22.34M OP For / 196.6K Against), effective immediately; the intake site opgrants.io is unreachable.
documents.summary: Optimism's Season 8 Growth Grants distributed a 6.29M OP Governance Fund budget against interop-ready TVL and interop transaction-fee metrics, selected by the Grants Council against a published public rubric. The season is closed and the Grants Council was dissolved by Token House vote on 15 July 2026.

documents.title: Scroll Community Grants
documents.description:
**Closed.** The Scroll Community Grants Support Program was a three-month pilot grant stream owned and run by the Scroll DAO Community Council, funding community activations worldwide — events, meetups, hackathons, and a catch-all 'Flex' category — that let local audiences explore the Scroll ecosystem, its products, assets and programs.

**Currency and size.** The award range is quoted in US dollars: grants of $200 to $10,000, with a hard cap of $10,000 USD per activation. The Council explicitly favoured smaller grassroots activations with reasonable budgets over lavish gatherings. The pilot's own funding pot was denominated separately in the Scroll token, at SCR 312,500 — because that is a different unit from the award range, the document currency here is USD and the SCR pot is recorded in text only.

**Process — correction to the stated turnaround.** Applications were evaluated on a rolling basis, but the published approval time is **within 30 days of application**, not 7 days. The Council clarified on the forum that the 30-day figure is a commitment to give every applicant timely feedback, not a requirement that every proposal take 30 days. Applicants submitted a milestone-broken-down budget; the initial payment is equal to or less than 30% of the overall budget, with the last payout conditional on submitting a final report. Grants above $2,000 required KYC/KYB, and all applicants signed standard AML statements in the form.

**Dates.** Applications closed 19 December 2025 (23:59). Funded activities had to be implemented and finished by 31 January 2026. The application page now reads 'Applications Closed — The deadline for this program has passed. New applications are no longer being accepted.'

**No later round.** No successor round or second season of the Community Grants Support Program has been posted on forum.scroll.io; the most recent forum activity runs to June 2026 with no renewal.

**Reporting.** Grantees deliver photos, video or social posts that Scroll can amplify, plus a brief recap on the governance forum. Regions covered by a Scroll Local Node with Local Node endorsement are funded from the Local Nodes budget instead.
documents.summary: Scroll DAO's Community Council ran a three-month pilot funding community activations (events, meetups, hackathons, flex) at $200-$10,000 USD each from an SCR 312,500 pot, with rolling review and approval within 30 days. Applications closed 19 December 2025, activities had to finish by 31 January 2026, and the application page now reports applications closed with no successor round posted.

documents.eligibility: Community organizers from all over the world are welcome to apply — whether you've been hosting local meetups, organizing a university club, running workshops for builders, or anything of a similar nature. In-person, virtual and hybrid events are all accepted, and collaborations across different local communities or with sponsors are encouraged. Grants above $2,000 require KYC/KYB verification, and all applicants sign standard AML statements through the application form. Where a request falls inside a Scroll Local Node region with the Local Node's endorsement, the Community Council funds it from the Local Nodes budget rather than the Community Grants budget.

⚡ Hack on Hills 8.0

The Age of Autonomous Agents

Welcome to Hack on Hills 8.0, the flagship 48-hour hackathon hosted by the App Team, NIT Hamirpur.

Over the years, Hack on Hills has grown into one of North India's largest student-run hackathons, bringing together thousands of developers, designers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts from across the country.

This edition explores a defining shift in technology: the rise of autonomous agents.

As AI systems evolve from tools that generate content to systems that can reason, plan, and execute tasks, we stand at the beginning of a new computing paradigm. Hack on Hills 8.0 invites participants to build products, platforms, and experiences that leverage this transformation to solve real-world problems.

Whether you're building intelligent agents, decentralized applications, sustainable technology solutions, or entirely new ideas, this is your opportunity to turn ambitious concepts into working products.

---

💡 Tracks

🤖 AI & Autonomous Agents

Build systems capable of reasoning, planning, decision-making, and autonomous execution.

⛓️ Blockchain & Web3

Develop decentralized applications, protocols, and infrastructure for the next generation of the internet.

🌱 Sustainability & Social Impact

Create technology solutions addressing environmental, social, and community challenges.

🚀 Open Innovation

Explore bold ideas beyond predefined categories and build solutions that create meaningful impact.

---

⚙️ Format & Eligibility

Team Size: 2-4 Members

Shortlisting: Based on participant profiles and application review

Finals: 48-hour in-person hackathon at NIT Hamirpur

Participants will collaborate, prototype, and present their projects before a panel of industry experts, mentors, and judges.

---

🏆 Prizes & Sponsor Tracks

Hack on Hills 8.0 features a prize pool, sponsor challenges, and ecosystem bounties designed to recognize outstanding innovation across multiple domains.

documents.title: Prezenti Anchor Pool
documents.description:
Season 2 Anchor Open Round, the open-application pool of Prezenti, Celo's community-run direct grants programme. **This round is now closed**: it ran 25 February 2026 – 30 June 2026 and the application form at anchor.prezenti.xyz now returns "This form is now closed — the form can't receive new submissions at this moment" (checked 2026-08-11).

**Outcome.** Anchor received 24 applications and funded 2 teams (BitGifty and TrenchVerse), each at $25,000, holding the traction bar rather than diluting criteria. $40,000 was reallocated out of Anchor mid-season on 5 May 2026 to capitalise a new Frontier pool for AI/agent-economy infrastructure, reducing Anchor's budget from $220,000 to $180,000; $130,015 was left uncommitted at season close and has been redeployed into Season 3.

**Grant terms.** One-off grants paid in USDm (the USD-pegged stablecoin Prezenti holds, obtained by converting its CELO disbursement through Mento), split 20% at project onset and 80% after agreed delivery, with KYC and a signed contract with Prezenti, and four months from contract signature to delivery. Applications moved from Charmverse to Tally Forms in May 2026 after Charmverse ceased trading; old Charmverse links are inactive.

**Stage-based grant sizes.** Stage 2 (Valora apps, Mini apps; 10K–100K est. daily transactions) ~$25k; Stage 3 (seed-stage or scaled products with traction; 100k–500k) ~$50k; Stage 4 (mature ecosystem apps; 500k+) case-by-case.

**Decision process.** The Prezenti review team scores proposals against a published rubric (alignment, open-source commitment, demo quality, team, metrics/KPIs, correct stage, demand understanding, financial plan, plus a discretionary factor) and reaches a final decision by internal consensus vote. Outcomes are typically returned around 4 weeks from submission, on a rolling basis, notified first by email to the lead applicant. 100% of rejected Season 2 applicants received tailored, rubric-tied feedback.

**Successor.** A Season 3 plan was posted to the Celo governance forum on 23 July 2026, continuing Anchor alongside Boost and Frontier and funded by redeploying held funds rather than a new treasury draw. As of 2026-08-11 the Anchor form has not reopened.
documents.summary: The Anchor Pool funds teams with real traction driving Celo ecosystem growth.

documents.title: Prezenti Mint Round
documents.description:
The Mint Round was an open round of Prezenti's Celo grant funding, following approval of the CeloPG H2 2024 funding. **It is closed** — applications ran from 1 October 2024 until 15 November 2024, and the Charmverse application space used to run it no longer exists (Charmverse ceased trading in May 2026; Prezenti's application links now point to Tally Forms for its current pools).

**Three grant types were offered, all denominated in cUSD:**

- **MICRO — $2,000 cUSD.** For one-off contributions that significantly enhance the Celo community: financial assistance to projects at the very start of their journey, or retroactive funding for those who have already made notable contributions — community management, open-source code contributions, governance and educational content.
- **PILOT — $10,000 cUSD.** For new projects yet to build and deploy a feasibility study, pilot, low-fidelity prototype or MVP. Small ticket size for getting something off the ground; applicants are expected to deliver at least to testnet (if technical) at a quality that could plausibly continue if the pilot succeeds. Projects must open-source their code and communicate what they learned. Priority to public-goods-style projects over commercial enterprises, though the latter is not disqualifying.
- **GROWTH — $25,000 cUSD.** For incremental features for ecosystem mainstays or public goods. VC-funded, private, for-profit companies are not disqualified as a hard rule if they are clearly delivering something pivotal to the community.

At the time the round opened, Prezenti reported having received over 300 applications and granted $1.2M cUSD across more than 70 grants.

documents.title: Devlynix Buildathon 1.0
documents.description:
Welcome to Devlynix Buildathon 1.0, an asynchronous, weekend-long mini-hackathon designed specifically to help you transition from watching tutorials to building practical, real-world projects.

This hackathon focuses on the "Idea-to-MVP Sprint" model. We aren't looking for perfect code; we are looking for strong problem-solving, clean design, and a solid technical approach.

# **⚠️ IMPORTANT: MANDATORY STEP**

All official announcements, squad formations, and shortlisting results will be shared EXCLUSIVELY on our WhatsApp handles. Joining both is mandatory for participation.

👉 Join our WhatsApp Channel: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VbCzGzaJpe8chzjL0w1F
👉 Join our Community Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EJrdn43jObx00BKnp444Rj

# ​📅 **Event Overview**

**Format:** 48-Hour Asynchronous Online Hackathon
**Team Size**: 1 to 4 Members per Squad
**Goal:** Build a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) addressing specific community tech challenges.

# 🛠️ The Challenge: Choose Your Problem Statement
Squads must select one of the following real-world challenges to solve. Your goal is to build a functional MVP with a clean User Interface.

> **1. The Developer Proof-of-Work Platform 🚀**
Many developers build great projects but lose them in scattered GitHub repositories. Build a centralized showcase directory where developers can host their deployed projects, tag their tech stack, and attach demo videos. Include filtering options (e.g., MERN, Web3, AI) for easy discovery.

>**2. The "Execution-First" Accountability Tracker 🔥**
Students often get stuck in "tutorial hell." Build a web dashboard that tracks a user's daily or weekly "build streak" based on actual project execution. The app should prompt users with "What did you code today?", visualize their consistency, and reward them with milestones.

>**3. The Skill-Based Teammate Matchmaker 🤝**
Finding the right teammates for hackathons or side projects is a major hurdle. Design a user-directory system where individuals can create profiles highlighting their specific skills (e.g., UI/UX, React, AI) and proficiency levels. Implement a search and filter mechanism to connect users.

> **4. The Crowdsourced Learning Vault 📚**
The internet is flooded with scattered resources. Build an organized, community-driven resource hub where users can submit and categorize high-quality links, tools, and guides. Include an upvote/downvote system so the best resources naturally rise to the top.

>**5. The Micro-Event & Submission Portal 🎯**
Small tech communities struggle to manage asynchronous events through chaotic group chats. Create a streamlined event dashboard displaying hackathon details, rules, and deadlines. It must feature a dedicated submission portal where teams can upload their final deliverables.

# 🎯 What You Need to Submit (The Deliverables)
To successfully complete the hackathon, your squad must submit the following three items:

 > **1. The Website MVP (Minimum Viable Product)**

**Build What You Can:** If you are a beginner, building just a clean, functional frontend MVP is completely fine. If you have the skills, you are highly encouraged to build the full-stack version (Frontend + Backend/Database)!

> **2. The Pitch Video (Max 10 Minutes)**

This is your final presentation! Record your screen and your voice.
**How to do it:** Walk us through your PPT first, and then give a live demo of your Website MVP.
**The Vibe:** Be confident! Explain your thought process, why you designed the UI a certain way, and how the code logic works.

# 📅 Buildathon 1.0: Official Timeline
**Phase 1: Registration & Concept Submission**
Date: 4th May
Duration: 24 Hours
Task: Register your team on Devfolio and start working on any problem statement given above.

**Phase 2: The 48-Hour Build Sprint**
Task: Start coding your MVP (Minimum Viable Product). This is the main development phase where you build your frontend/full-stack solution.
Submission: Keep your Deployed Website Link.

**Phase 3: Final Submission & Video Pitch**
Final Deliverables: 
1. Deployed Website Link. (In Project Links)
2. GitHub Repo URL. (In Project Links)
3. Final Video Demo (Max 10 Minutes):(YouTube link)

Important: The Devfolio submission portal will automatically close at 11:59 PM on 6th May.

**📅 Important Instructions for Participants:**

Strict Deadlines: Submissions after the round deadline will lead to automatic disqualification.

Communication: All shortlisting announcements will be made via the official Devlynix WhatsApp group and Devfolio notifications.

# 📊 Evaluation Criteria
Judges will evaluate your submissions out of 100 Points based on these 4 pillars:

**Problem-Solution Fit (25 Points):** How practical and realistic is your solution?
**UI/UX & Design (25 Points):** Is the layout user-friendly, clean, and adhering to the 'Silent Coder' aesthetic?
**Technical Logic (25 Points):** How functional is the code, or how clearly is the technical architecture defined?
**The Final Pitch (25 Points):** How well was the product explained and demonstrated in the video?

*Get ready to build. Good luck, Squads! Let's build something awesome. 🛠️🔥*

**Prizes, all of them non-monetary.** The event publishes six prize entries and every one of them carries a zero amount: Grand Prize (a shoutout on the organiser's LinkedIn page, a Certificate of Excellence and one-to-one portfolio mentorship), Runner-Up Squad (a community Wall of Fame place and a digital Certificate of Merit), Best UI/UX Award, Pure Coder Award, 2nd Runner Up, and a Certificate of Participation for a hundred entrants. There is no cash pool to record, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.

documents.title: Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (UFSF)
documents.description:
**Open — and not a single closed cohort.** The Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (UFSF) provides up to 100% coverage of security-audit costs for projects building in the Uniswap ecosystem, delivered through Areta's audit marketplace.

**Correction to the deadline.** The 7 May 2026 date on this record is a single monthly cut-off, not the end of the program. UFSF runs a **monthly cohort system**: applications close on the **7th of each month at 23:59 UTC**, and the application form **stays open year-round**. An application that misses a month's cut-off automatically enters the next month's cohort. The Uniswap Foundation still links this form directly from its own homepage.

**Fund size.** UFSF is a **$1M subsidy pool**, announced on the Uniswap governance forum as "a fund size of USD $1M created through a Uniswap Foundation grant" that "will subsidize up to 100% of the auditing fees of security services for eligible projects building Uniswap v4 hooks", and restated at Cohort 2 as "a $1M initiative to support security audits for projects building in the Uniswap ecosystem". That $1M is the pool across cohorts, not a per-project cap: "up to 100% of audit costs" is a coverage rule with no number attached, and no per-project ceiling is published anywhere, so this record carries a budget and no maximum award. The Foundation's grant to the operator is a different and larger figure — $1,200,000, covering the subsidy pool plus program management — and is not the fund size. **Recency caveat:** the $1M was announced at launch in October 2024 and last restated in February 2025; every monthly cohort post since, through August 2026, repeats the coverage rule without restating or topping up a fund size.

**Application limits.** Each project may apply to UFSF a maximum of 3 times in total; reapplying with materially new information, or consenting to carry an application forward into the next cohort, each counts toward that cap.

**Marketplace route.** Applicants who book an audit through the Areta marketplace are automatically considered for a retroactive subsidy in the next two cohorts, and a campaign incentive makes every 3rd project that accepts an offer on the marketplace eligible for cashback of up to $10,000 (subject to availability and terms). Applicants who are not booking an audit right now can either reapply with new information or carry the application forward.

**Compliance.** Applicants must accept the Head Agreement and Application Conditions at application time and may be required to execute the Foundation's Grant Agreement as part of a KYC/KYB process following a positive subsidy decision.

**Support channel.** Applicants coordinate through the UFSF Telegram group at https://t.me/UFSF_Applicants.
documents.summary: The Uniswap Foundation Security Fund covers up to 100% of smart-contract audit costs for Uniswap-ecosystem teams via vetted auditors on Areta. It runs monthly cohorts — applications close the 7th of each month at 23:59 UTC — and the form stays open year-round, with missed applications rolling into the next cohort. Each project may apply a maximum of three times.

documents.title: Yellow Acceleration #2
documents.description:
Yellow Acceleration #2 is a growth program for startups building with blockchain technologies, run by Yellow (the Layer-3 state-channel clearing network behind the Yellow SDK / NeoDAX). Intake is deliberately low-friction: the published form opens with "Thanks for your interest in building with Yellow! Whether you already have a clear idea or are still figuring things out - that's totally OK!" and asks applicants only to "express your intent to apply to the acceleration program", after which "our team will get back to you shortly."

The form collects name, email, Telegram handle, whether the applicant has a team, team/company name, a short description of the team and of what is being built, a GitHub or website link, availability to pitch online, and availability to pitch offline "during DAPPConference Berlin June 16-17" in the event of selection to the Final. It also asks applicants to confirm they have joined the Yellow Telegram community.

**Prizes.** Yellow published 25,000 USD in prizes for this wave, twice and only on its own X account: "We're accepting applications to Wave 2 of the Yellow Acceleration program … With 25k USD in prizes!" (23 April 2026) and "Applications for round 2 are open now, with 25K USD to be won + ongoing support channels." (1 May 2026). Both posts link to exactly the application form on this record, which is what ties the figure to this program. Both phrasings are pool-level ("in prizes", "to be won"), so this is the round's total rather than a per-team award: no split by place, no per-team cap, and no equity or token terms are published anywhere, so no award range is recorded.

Nothing else is published: no cohort size, cohort dates or application deadline appear on the form or on yellow.org. The other monetary figure Yellow publishes for builders belongs to a *different* programme — the Yellow Builder Program at yellow.org/build, which offers "up to $50K for your project" against four milestones (M0 Acceptance, M1 Kickoff, M2 Live, M3 Scaling) and has its own intake at forms.yellow.org/build. The two should not be conflated.

As of 2026-08-11 the acceleration form is still live and accepting responses (no closure notice, Submit button present), but the offline Final it points at — DAPP Conference Berlin, June 16–17 — has already passed, and Yellow has published no cohort roster, selection outcome or Round 3 announcement.

documents.title: Arbitrum Open House — London
documents.description:
Arbitrum Open House — London is the London leg of Arbitrum's global builder programme, hosted by the Arbitrum Foundation and run on HackQuest, with the IRL component delivered in partnership with Encode Club.

It has two parts. First, the "Arbitrum Open House London: Online Buildathon" — a 3-week online build sprint (tech stack Solidity and Rust) with a total prize pool of 115,000 USDC, split across three reward pots of 70,000 / 30,000 / 15,000 USDC. Registration and submission opened 2026-03-24, registration closed 2026-06-12, submissions closed 2026-06-14, and rewards/winners were announced 2026-06-17. It drew 782 registered participants and 273 submitted projects.

Second, the IRL Founder House in London on 10–12 July 2026, 120 spots, described as offering "Direct access to and feedback from the Arbitrum Foundation, Offchain Labs, and Open House Sponsors", "Product, technical, go-to-market, and fundraising guidance", "Hands-on workshops covering the tools and infrastructure needed to build and scale on Arbitrum", "Dedicated time to build alongside high-quality teams" and "Opportunities to connect with investors, partners, and ecosystem leaders", with "$300,000 in prizes and grants across multiple tracks". The 415,000 USD figure previously carried on this record reconciles as 115,000 (buildathon) + 300,000 (Founder House).

Open House also ran NYC (30,000 USD prize pool, 514 participants) and an APAC Mini Hackathon (4,000 USD, 232 participants); both are shown as Ended.

As of 2026-08-11 both legs are over: the HackQuest listing carries currentStatus REGISTER_CLOSE and VOTING_CLOSE with winners announced, and the Founder House dates are in the past.

documents.title: Q402 Grant Program
documents.description:
The Q402 Grant Program supports builders developing gasless Web3 user experiences. **Awards are relay credits, not cash grants** — prepaid transaction-relay capacity on Q402's infrastructure, quoted in US dollars and in the number of transactions the credit covers.

**Tiers as published**

| Tier | Credit | Transactions | Also includes | Who it's for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed | $500 relay credit | up to 10,000 txs | priority support, Q402 partner badge | "Early-stage projects exploring gasless and agentic UX" |
| Builder | $2,000 relay credit | up to 50,000 txs | co-marketing opportunity, direct Telegram access, custom chain configuration | "Live products scaling gasless and agent payments" |
| Ecosystem | Custom | Unlimited | custom credit pool, revenue share model, joint press release, board advisory access | "Strategic partners and infrastructure builders" |

**Application process.** Apply directly on the grant page; applications are reviewed within 3 to 5 business days. Follow-up is by email (business@quackai.ai) or Telegram. No deadline is published — intake is rolling.

**About the platform.** Q402 is gasless payment infrastructure for AI agents and Web3 apps, built by Quack AI. It lets users send stablecoins (USDC, USDT, RLUSD) without paying gas, using EIP-712 signatures and EIP-7702, and exposes payments to agents such as Claude and Codex through a single Model Context Protocol tool call. Status: Live on mainnet across BNB Chain, Ethereum, Mantle, Avalanche, Injective, X Layer, Stable, Monad, Scroll, Arbitrum, Base and Robinhood Chain.

## **Hack Boldly, Create in Chaos – Hack&Chill 3.0**

Hack&Chill 3.0 is a multi-day **offline hackathon** organized by GDGC ADGIPS, where innovation emerges from chaos. Participants collaborate, build impactful solutions, and compete in an intense coding environment guided by mentors and industry experts. ---

### 📝 **Online Screening Round (Pre-Hackathon)**
- Participants register on Devfolio  
- Each team must submit a short PPT explaining their idea  [Submit your PPT here](https://forms.gle/tR8uWh2PtTnACBoZA)
- Submissions are evaluated based on innovation, clarity, and feasibility  
- **Top 50 teams are shortlisted** to proceed to the hackathon  

---

- 25 shortlisted teams begin hacking  
- Teams start building their prototypes  
- Mentors conduct dedicated mentoring sessions  
- Projects are reviewed and evaluated  

---

### ⚡ **Day 2 – Hackathon (Batch 2)**
- Remaining 25 shortlisted teams begin hacking  
- Teams build and refine their prototypes  
- Mentors provide guidance and conduct mentoring rounds  
- Projects are reviewed and evaluated  

---

### 🧠 **Mentor Evaluation Round**
- Projects are assessed on innovation, feasibility, and implementation  
- **Top 10 teams are selected** for the final round  

---

### 🏆 **Final Day – Grand Finale**
- Top 10 teams present their projects to the judging panel  
- Winners are announced  

---

## 🎁 **Prizes**

- 🎉 Additional rewards including swags and in-kind prizes

documents.title: Web3 X Incubation Program — Batch 07
documents.description:
Batch 07 of the Web3 X Incubation Program, an execution-focused 6-week online incubation run by Web3 X ("Since 2023, Web3 X has supported builders across the global Web3 ecosystem"; the site claims 40+ startups incubated, $12M+ raised by alumni, 25+ ecosystem partnerships, 300+ investor connections and 10+ exchange listings supported).

Batch 07 schedule as published: REGISTRATION 15.03 – 15.04; KICK-OFF May; PHASE 2 INVESTMENT TRAINING May – June; DEMO DAY August 2026. The core training is 6 weeks; all sessions are conducted online "to allow global teams to participate, with additional opportunities for in-person networking during major Web3 events".

What teams get: "The Opportunity To Invest Up To 50,000 USD After Graduation"; "Grant upto 100.000 USD and further support such as Investment, Liquidity, MKT, Listing from Ecosystem Partner"; "Exclusive Credits And Discounts Worth 500,000 USD From Our Partners"; an "Offline - DemoDay in one of the biggest blockchain event in Asia"; "Fast Track to other Incubation program such as MVB from BNB chain"; mentorship, networking, and practical instruction in legal, listing, market making, tokenomics and fundraising.

Cohort workshop curriculum: Kick-off; Finding the right co-founder; Legal — how to set up a Web3 company; Pricing & Tokenomics; MKT and Go-To-Market in Web3; How Market Makers work; VC score cards; Closing ceremony & next steps. Demo Day track: VC insights panel; blockchain foundation insights panel; presenting effectively; pitching practice; security in Web3; metrics & benchmarks.

Terms: "There are no upfront fees to join Web3 X… In return for our support, investment access, and long-term partnership, we may request a small allocation of equity or tokens, depending on your project structure and fundraising plans."

As of 2026-08-11 the registration window (15.03 – 15.04) has closed and Batch 07 is at its Demo Day stage; the page still carries an active Apply Now form and no later batch has replaced Batch 07.

documents.title: Regenesis Season 1 Grants
documents.description:
The Regenesis Grants Program funds builders who ship. Each season targets specific needs in the Decentraland ecosystem — Season 1's themes were mobile-optimized content (Content Development domain) and AI-assisted tooling (Tech Ecosystem domain). Projects are scoped, milestone-tracked, and open source from day one, with a maximum of 90 days from approval to final delivery.

**Season 1 is closed.** The site's own FAQ states: "No — Season 1 applications closed on April 24, 2026." Season 1 ran April – July 2026: submissions opened 1 April, closed 24 April, evaluation 20 April – 1 May, projects kicked off 1–8 May, delivery deadline 31 July. Seven projects were awarded a total of $32,250; six went into active delivery through August 2026 (Flagtag $7,750; Decentraland Social $6,000, cancelled before kickoff; The Pixel Arcade $4,000; Goal Legends Arena $4,000; Doge Hunt $4,000; AdventureLand $3,500; Candy Sheep Meadow $3,000). The operator's own caveat: "This is a pilot season — we're testing the process and expect it to evolve."

**Season 2 is upcoming**, scheduled July – November 2026 with submissions opening in August 2026, close date TBD and themes to be announced. As of 2026-08-11 the site still reads "Season 2 is on the way — stay tuned for the next call for proposals", so Season 2 intake had not yet opened.

**Five-step process.** 1) Submit your proposal via the application form. 2) AI agent review — the proposal enters a structured review by specialized AI agents (Technical Feasibility, Creativity & Art, Gameplay & Mechanics, Marketing & Reach), each getting a dedicated forum thread where they post questions and clarification requests that applicants are expected to answer. 3) Human evaluation — the Regenesis Labs team reviews the AI assessments and takes the agents' recommendations into consideration when making the final funding decision. 4) Decision & kickoff — decisions are communicated within roughly one month after the submission window closes; approved projects are funded and start their 90-day build. 5) Build & deliver — payment is released against milestone checkpoints; missing two consecutive milestones may terminate the grant.

**Payment.** Up to $15,000 USD equivalent in MANA, Decentraland's native token, per project, paid against milestones.

Note: a season may choose not to fund at all if submissions don't meet the quality bar.
documents.summary: Season 1 of the DCL Regenesis Labs Grants Program: up to $15,000 USD equivalent in MANA for small, focused, open-source Decentraland projects delivered in 90 days, themed on mobile-optimized content and AI-assisted tooling. Applications closed 24 April 2026; seven projects were awarded a total of $32,250.

operatingOrganizations.name: DCL Regenesis Labs
operatingOrganizations.description: "The execution arm of the Decentraland DAO — turning community decisions into consistent delivery." It manages operations, treasury, and the Regenesis Grants Program funding builders who make Decentraland better. Publishes a transparency site and a dedicated Decentraland forum category.

documents.eligibility: Individual developers, small teams, and studios anywhere in the world can apply; the requirement is the ability to deliver within 90 days. You don't need to already be building in Decentraland — external studios and developers exploring it for the first time are welcome. Good fit: you have a specific, scoped idea, not a vague concept; you can deliver a working product in 90 days; you're building for mobile or creating AI-powered tools; you're comfortable working in the open (open source); you have relevant experience as a solo dev, team, or studio; you understand Decentraland or are willing to learn fast. Proposals must match the current season's themes. Funded work is open source from day one.
documents.additionalReferences: Grants site: https://grants.dclregenesislabs.xyz/ · Application form: https://forms.gle/9ZSx45cpwE4qdt3G9 · Grants contact: grantsprogram@dclregenesislabs.xyz · DCL Regenesis Labs transparency site: https://transparency.dclregenesislabs.xyz/ (dclregenesislabs.xyz redirects here) · Regenesis Labs forum category: https://forum.decentraland.org/c/regenesis-labs/18 · Decentraland governance: https://decentraland.org/governance/ · Season 2 is scheduled July–November 2026 with submissions opening August 2026 and close date TBD.
documents.prerequisites: A clear project summary; the problem or opportunity you're addressing; scoped deliverables; a 90-day roadmap with milestones; a budget breakdown tied to deliverables; measurable success metrics; and team background and relevant experience. A strong proposal states the gap it fills and exactly what will ship. Applicants are also expected to answer the AI reviewers' follow-up questions on their proposal's dedicated forum thread.

sponsoringOrganizations.description: The DAO governing Decentraland. The Regenesis Grants Program is "Backed by the DAO. Managed by DCL Regenesis Labs." Grants are paid in MANA, Decentraland's native token.

documents.title: Arbitrum DDA — Developer Tooling on Arbitrum One and Nova
documents.description:
The Developer Tooling domain of the Arbitrum DAO's Delegated Domain Allocation (DDA) program, administered on Questbook. An elected domain allocator — listed as @Flook_Eth — owns the domain budget, publishes its priorities and decides each award; the domain is shown with Status "Live" and "Available $132k", which is the domain's remaining envelope rather than a per-award cap. The per-grant soft cap is stated separately as 25,000 ARB.

The domain page frames scope as four buckets. "Back to basics": essential infrastructure for asset visualisation and network interaction — e.g. an RPC built on Alchemy infrastructure, or translation of successful projects' documentation into Mandarin, Japanese, Spanish and French — plus foundations that let dApps and protocols run their own metrics systems, on the explicit view that "Total Value Locked (TVL) may not be the most appropriate metric". "Bring something cool from another chain to Arbitrum": toolkits and SDKs that make Lens-, Farcaster- or Push-style applications buildable on Arbitrum, including better documentation and MVPs for B2B SaaS-shaped functionality. "Addressing the current challenges of Arbitrum": centralization, ecosystem development and security — documentation to help build sequencers, developer SDKs for dApps "we've never heard of", and scanners that surface and improve vulnerabilities in deployed contracts. "DevRel": developer-first projects that streamline communication between developers and ecosystem stakeholders.

Worked examples the allocator publishes: IDEs for Arbitrum's chains (editor, debugger, compiler, deployer, or Arbitrum support added to existing products); SDKs and libraries for interacting with Arbitrum's smart-contract platform plus testing, deployment and monitoring tooling; testing and debugging frameworks across environments; monitoring and analytics tools covering gas usage, transaction times and user engagement; documentation and tutorial portals covering Arbitrum's API; and community forums and support channels for Arbitrum developers. Projects that lower the barrier for new developers — tutorials, articles, boilerplate, starter projects — are explicitly in scope.

Evaluation: "Proposals in this domain are typically reviewed directly by the domain allocator. Depending on the proposal content, the domain allocator may consult with allocator(s) in relevant domain(s) and may invite other allocator(s) to provide additional review." The rubric is five items each scored 0–5: Team experience; Novelty and quality of the idea; Relevance to our ecosystem; Completeness of the plan; Feasibility of goals and timeline. "Proposals that score highly in the evaluation rubric are more likely to be funded, but there is no minimum threshold number of points for funding and no threshold that guarantees funding. Grant decisions are heavily influenced by the evaluation rubric but also take into consideration the balancing of project areas."

Disbursement is milestone-gated: "All milestones are required to be filled in disbursements following the following disbursement schedule (template): Compound Milestone Tranches - Alcancía.pdf". There is no round deadline — proposals are read as they arrive.

**Go-live.** The DDA program "went live on the 5th of October" 2023 with $800k across four domains, of which this is one; Questbook's Phase 2 continuation request on the Arbitrum forum is what dates it. Both original domains in this corpus carry that same go-live as `postedAt`, because the four domains opened together and none of them was announced separately.

fundingDetails.scope: Developer tooling, open-source dApps and documentation for Arbitrum One and Arbitrum Nova, across four published buckets. (1) Back to basics — essential infrastructure for asset visualisation and network interaction, including RPC systems built on Alchemy infrastructure and translation of ecosystem documentation into Mandarin, Japanese, Spanish and French; plus foundations enabling dApps and protocols to run their own metrics systems, on the stated view that TVL is often the wrong measure of alignment with growth OKRs. (2) Bring something cool from another chain to Arbitrum — toolkits and SDKs enabling Lens-, Farcaster- or Push-style applications, improved documentation and MVPs for B2B-SaaS-shaped functionality. (3) Addressing the current challenges of Arbitrum — centralization, ecosystem development and security: documentation to help build sequencers, developer SDKs for novel dApps, and scanners that surface and improve vulnerabilities in contracts deployed on chain. (4) DevRel — developer-first projects that streamline communication between developers and ecosystem stakeholders. Concrete product ideas the allocator names: IDEs (code editor, debugger, compiler, deployer, or Arbitrum support added to existing IDEs); SDKs and libraries for interacting with Arbitrum's smart-contract platform plus testing, deployment and monitoring tools; testing and debugging frameworks across multiple environments; monitoring and analytics tools covering gas usage, transaction times and user engagement; documentation and tutorial portals covering Arbitrum's API; and community forums and support channels for Arbitrum developers. Work that makes Arbitrum's chains more accessible to new developers — educational resources, tutorials, articles, boilerplate code and starter projects — is explicitly in scope. Out of scope: proposals belonging to the other DDA domains, which have their own allocators.
requirements: The work targets Arbitrum One or Arbitrum Nova.
The proposal is broken into milestones the allocator can review and disburse against.
All milestones must be filled in as disbursements following the domain's disbursement-schedule template ("Compound Milestone Tranches - Alcancía.pdf").
Requests should respect the domain's per-grant soft cap of 25,000 ARB.

documents.title: Arbitrum DDA — Education, Community Growth and Events
documents.description:
The Education, Community Growth and Events domain of the Arbitrum DAO's Delegated Domain Allocation (DDA) program, administered on Questbook. The elected domain allocator is listed as @SEED Latam, reachable through the domain's Discord invite. The domain shows Status "Live" with "Available $120k" — the remaining envelope, not a per-award cap.

The allocator states its posture plainly: "We recognize that communities and the educational realm play an essential role in the growth of an ecosystem… However, we're also aware that this domain is one of the most challenging to evaluate its real impact or the quality of its content. We know it can be susceptible to opportunistic practices, such as 'farming', and sometimes the budgets presented may be excessive. It's vital for us to adopt a critical approach to ensure funds are allocated to initiatives that genuinely have a positive impact on Arbitrum."

Four funding verticals are published: Organization of Hackathons (the primary vertical and "our main focus"), for web3 hackathons in Arbitrum One, Arbitrum Nova and Arbitrum Orbit ecosystems, with "special attention to those hackathons that promote the development of tools and products using Stylus"; Initiatives for Institutional Community Growth, connecting and strengthening the Arbitrum community in universities and educational institutions and reaching beyond software development into Economics, Law, Political Science and others, including innovations in academic development in collaboration with Arbitrum DAO and governance; Educational Materials and Workshops, long-lasting tutorials and videos covering Arbitrum One, Nova, Orbit and Stylus in visual, written or web formats, multilingual, and "vital that these resources be freely accessible and offered for free"; and IRL educational events where "Arbitrum stands out as the protagonist", with a stated preference for smaller gatherings of 30–60 participants in emerging or unconventional regions.

Explicit exclusions: "In the educational branch, we won't back sensationalist materials or those about airdrops, ARB token quotations, or fleeting news. Our mission is to promote consistent, long-term educational content." On events: "we won't support two consecutive events from one region or the same country - this is obviously subject to demand", and content value is prioritised "rather than purely promotional strategies".

Six evaluation criteria are published: Team Composition and Experience (web3 plus "a solid and verifiable background in web2", trustworthy individuals with an impeccable reputation, no fraudulent behaviour); Innovation and Quality of the Idea (high quality, durable, freely accessible, academic rather than advertising, university collaborations valued); Budget and Plan Depth (justified budgets with a thorough breakdown; excessive or unrelated expenses will be scrutinised; applicants urged to receive funds through a multisig "not only as a security measure but also to ensure resources aren't under the exclusive control of a single address"); Roadmap and Milestones (well-defined, realistic, feasible; ambiguous proposals will not be considered; milestones serve as benchmarks for the community to monitor progress); Impact, Outcomes and Metrics (robust assessment methods, open and consistent communication with the Arbitrum community, tangible on-chain or off-chain outcomes, published metrics after a set period); and Long-Term Perspective (sustained vision, no short-lived initiatives).

Proposals are read as they arrive; there is no round deadline.

**Go-live.** The DDA program "went live on the 5th of October" 2023 with $800k across four domains, of which this is one; Questbook's Phase 2 continuation request on the Arbitrum forum is what dates it. Both original domains in this corpus carry that same go-live as `postedAt`, because the four domains opened together and none of them was announced separately.

documents.description:
A Request for Proposals run by the Ethereum Foundation's Ecosystem Support Program (ESP) in the run-up to Devcon 8 (3–6 November 2026, Jio World Centre, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai, India).

The program "supports grassroots initiatives that contribute to the Ethereum ecosystem's growth and resilience ahead of Devcon 8… empowering local projects, builders, and ecosystem contributors to create meaningful spaces for learning, experimentation, and coordination, both online and in-person." Supported formats are "meetups, bootcamps, hackathons, roundtables, academic collaborations, and other formats" that bring new people into Ethereum, strengthen connections across open source communities and the broader technology ecosystem, and encourage hands-on participation and knowledge sharing around CROPS.

Stated need: expanding access to Ethereum for new and diverse audiences and lowering barriers to entry through education, experimentation and local initiatives; bridging Ethereum with open source communities; and "Promoting and putting into practice Ethereum's core values, including: Censorship Resistance, Open Source, Privacy, and Security, through hands-on experiences" — the CROPS acronym the RFP tests applicants against.

Support on offer: "Up to $300 USD in financial support"; "Visibility and amplification across Devcon channels"; "Non-financial support (connections, guidance, coordination)"; and "Limited Devcon tickets (free or discounted), based on contribution and availability", capped at 5 per request. documents.title: RFP: Reboot the Gitcoin Community for the 3.3 Era
documents.description:
A vendor solicitation posted to the Gitcoin DAO governance forum on 13 May 2026 by owocki. Header block as published: "Issued by: Gitcoin DAO (sponsor: Kevin Owocki, ED) · Date issued: May 2026 · Proposals due: Rolling, first review June 1, 2026 · Engagement window: June 2026 – Q1 2027 (phased; see milestones) · Budget envelope: Open — propose your number. Bias toward lean, milestone-gated engagements over a single large retainer. · Submit to: kevin@gitcoin.co and/or post a response on gov.gitcoin.co".

Context given: "Gitcoin is entering its 3.3 era… The DAO controls ~$20M in treasury + matching pool; ~12M GTC is held by the DAO and needs to be re-delegated back to a real, engaged community of delegates. We are looking for one or more vendors / collectives / individuals to run a phased community reboot. You may bid on one, two, or all three. We expect to award multiple contracts."

WORKSTREAM A — DELEGATION: recruit 10–30 GTC delegates capable of carrying ~2.5M GTC of voting power (target ~100K–250K GTC per delegate, with a long tail). Proposal threshold is 150K GTC; quorum is 2.5M GTC (GovernorBravo 0x9d4c63565d5618310271bf3f3c01b2954c1d1639). Scope: build a candidate pipeline sourced from the existing Gitcoin community, allied DAOs (Optimism, Arbitrum, ENS, Protocol Guild, Octant), Ethereum public-goods orgs, AI-livelihood-aligned operators, regen/impact orgs and returning Gitcoin alumni; vet candidates against a public rubric covering mission alignment, governance track record, time commitment, conflicts, and geographic and ideological diversity; produce delegate profiles on Tally and gov.gitcoin.co; run delegate onboarding (GTC mechanics, treasury landscape, the 3.3 mission, open proposals, cadence expectations); and coordinate the delegation events themselves, matching candidates with GTC holders and getting the transactions executed. Deliverables: public rubric and selection process; 10–30 onboarded, publicly-profiled delegates with active GTC delegated; a live delegate roster with bios, conflicts and contact; a delegate orientation handbook (one-pager plus 30-min recorded onboarding); and a quarterly delegate health check. Success metrics: ≥ 2.5M GTC actively delegated to non-Foundation, non-multisig addresses within 90 days of contract start; no single delegate holding > 20% of active delegated supply; ≥ 70% of active delegates voting on at least 80% of proposals in their first 6 months. Gitcoin provides introductions (Foundation, Kyle Weiss, Owocki, existing top delegates), social amplification, coordination with Mathilda on contract/Governor parameters, and a pool of GTC the Foundation and Kevin are willing to delegate (subject to separate approval).

WORKSTREAM B — EDUCATION: re-onboard the community to Gitcoin 3.3 and open a first door for net-new audiences (AI-economy operators, livelihood-focused funders, post-Web3 builders). Scope: a 6–8 week educational series across at least three formats — weekly or biweekly Twitter/X Spaces of ~45–60 min (Kevin plus co-host explainers, debates with critics, deep-dives with builders), monthly async-friendly AMAs on gov.gitcoin.co or elsewhere with a written summary published within 48h, and one additional format of the bidder's choice (podcast, YouTube longform, in-person at events, IRL salons, workshops, university chapters); a canonical "Gitcoin 3.3 in 10 minutes" explainer in video and written form; an FAQ on gov.gitcoin.co absorbing questions surfaced in Spaces/AMAs; and 3–5 seeded third-party explainers. Deliverables: a published calendar of educational events; ≥ 20 Twitter Spaces and ≥ 6 AMAs over the 6-month engagement; the canonical explainer; a maintained FAQ with ≥ 50 entries; and 3–5 third-party content placements. Success metrics: cumulative attended-live audience across Spaces ≥ 15K and cumulative replays ≥ 100K; ≥ 100 new gov.gitcoin.co accounts and ≥ 100 new GTC delegations attributable to educational programming; ≥ 25 pieces of independent third-party content referencing Gitcoin 3.3; ≥ 10 inbound asks per month citing educational content as the entry point. Gitcoin provides Kevin's time (cap ~3 hrs/week public-facing), talent introductions, brand assets, and its forum and social channels.

WORKSTREAM C — CAMPAIGN: a launch campaign plan for Gitcoin 3.3, targeted at ~Q4 2026 / Q1 2027. Explicitly: "We are not procuring execution of the campaign today. We are procuring the campaign plan, with an option to execute pending mutual agreement closer to launch." The plan must cover an audience map (delegates, builders, funders, beneficiaries, press, allied DAOs, each with its call-to-action); narrative architecture over a ~6-week launch window with hero artifacts; a channel plan (X, Farcaster, podcasts, conference presence including Devcon, partner co-marketing, paid if justified, press); mechanism activation driving at least one measurable on-chain event; a risk plan covering low turnout, hostile takes, technical delay and AI-livelihood backlash; budget and team, with pricing for the plan separate from pricing for execution; and proposed KPIs. Deliverables: a written plan of 2–5 pages delivered no later than 90 days before target launch, one review session with Kevin, Mathilda, Julia, Ash and ≥ 2 advisors, and an optional bid to execute.

WHO THEY WANT: community-organizing operators with DAO governance experience; editorial/media collectives with crypto-native distribution and a record of moving narrative "(not just impressions)"; individual operators with deep Ethereum public-goods relationships; and cross-movement organizers from outside crypto (AI safety, livelihood/labor, post-growth, regen). Explicitly not fits: "pure paid-media agencies, 'growth hacking' shops, generic web3 marketing firms, anyone whose primary offer is follower count."

REVIEW PROCESS: "Rolling. First batch reviewed June 1, 2026 by Kevin + Mathilda + ≥ 1 advisor. Shortlisted vendors get a call. Decisions announced on gov.gitcoin.co."

The posting carries four open questions bidders are asked to address, and a standing caveat: "This RFP is a living document. It will be updated as the working groups (education: Julia; funding/recruitment: Mathilda; marketing: Ash) refine scope," plus a disclaimer that it "is for informative purposes only… reflects my personal views, not a decision or commitment by Gitcoin governance."

As of 2026-08-11 the forum thread is still titled "DRAFT - RFP: Reboot the Gitcoin Community for the 3.3 Era", carries no tags, and is neither closed nor archived. It has five posts; the last was 2026-06-05. Four public bid summaries have been posted (SEEDGov, Anode/Kaf, Tanisha Katara of Katara Consulting Group, and Eureka/Sixty), all bidding on Workstream A with partial bids on B and C. No award, shortlist or decision has been announced on the thread.

**The open budget is the RFP's design, not a missing field.** Beyond the header's "Budget envelope: Open — propose your number", the RFP pushes pricing onto bidders everywhere it could have set a ceiling: "Budget and milestone structure. Prefer milestone-gated payments"; "Budget and team. What you'd need to execute. Pricing for the plan should be separate from pricing for execution"; and, among its open questions, "What's your honest read on the MVP budget that produces real signal vs. theater?" No range, per-workstream cap or per-milestone amount appears anywhere. The only dollar figure in the document is context about the DAO's own finances (~$20M in treasury plus matching pool), not this engagement's envelope. Of the four bids posted to the thread, three state that the priced proposal went to the sponsor by email and one published its own ask — $5,000 total, split across two milestones — which is a bidder's price and not the program's, so nothing is recorded from it.
