Workstream C deliverables: a written campaign plan of 2–5 pages delivered no later than 90 days before the target launch date; one review session with Kevin, Mathilda, Julia, Ash and ≥ 2 advisors; optionally, a bid to execute the plan.

Workstream C success criterion: the plan must be readable and judged executable by Kevin and the working group, hand-offable to another vendor without losing critical context, and must explicitly address the three Dec-2027 KPIs.
No budget envelope is published: the proposal names its own price and justifies it, with a stated bias toward lean, milestone-gated engagements over a single large retainer.
The proposal states which of the three workstreams it covers.
The proposal is submitted to kevin@gitcoin.co and cross-posted publicly to the governance forum thread.

documents.additionalReferences: Forum thread (still titled "DRAFT - RFP: …", not closed or archived as of 2026-08-11): https://gov.gitcoin.co/t/draft-rfp-reboot-the-gitcoin-community-for-the-3-3-era/25256 · Submission email: kevin@gitcoin.co · Gitcoin GovernorBravo contract referenced for quorum and proposal threshold: 0x9d4c63565d5618310271bf3f3c01b2954c1d1639 · Public bid summaries posted to the thread: SEEDGov (2026-05-29), Anode/Kaf (2026-06-01), Tanisha Katara / Katara Consulting Group (2026-06-01), Eureka/Sixty (2026-06-05) · Gitcoin governance forum: https://gov.gitcoin.co/
documents.prerequisites: A proposal of at most 3 pages covering: which workstream(s) you are bidding on; team and relevant track record ("links > prose"); approach, including what you would do in the first 30 days; budget and milestone structure, with milestone-gated payments preferred; conflicts of interest (current GTC holdings, governance roles, competing engagements); and references (2–3 prior clients or collaborators Gitcoin can ask). Submit to kevin@gitcoin.co AND post a public response on gov.gitcoin.co — "we want the bids to be partly visible to the community we're rebuilding". Proposals are also asked to address four open questions: how to avoid a delegate base that is "just our existing inner circle wearing new hats"; how to re-engage former Gitcoin community members who left during the 2023–2025 wind-down without litigating the past; how educational content recruits non-crypto-native AI-livelihood operators without alienating the crypto-native delegate base; and "What's your honest read on the MVP budget that produces real signal vs. theater?"
documents.serviceAgreement: Phased engagement running June 2026 – Q1 2027, structured as milestone-gated contracts rather than a single large retainer. Multiple contracts are expected to be awarded across the three workstreams; Workstream C is procured as a plan first, with an option to execute pending mutual agreement closer to launch.

documents.title: Ecosystem Support Program (ESP)
documents.description:
The Ecosystem Support Program (ESP) is an ecosystem-development cluster inside the Ethereum Foundation made up of two teams: Grant Management (allocating resources to the projects most critical to Ethereum's resilience and usability) and Funding Coordination (making it simpler and faster for impactful projects to secure funding, including co-funding work with Octant, Gitcoin and ENS DAO).

ESP supports free, open-source, non-commercial work directed at builders rather than end users: Ethereum infrastructure, builder tooling, cryptographic research, education and community development.

**Application process (six steps, rolling, no deadline):**
1. **Browse** the Wishlist or the RFP list and find an item matching your expertise. Wishlist items name gaps and invite you to propose an approach; RFP items are more prescriptive and time-bound around a defined deliverable.
2. **Apply** with a proposal covering methodology, timeline and deliverables. You receive a confirmation email.
3. **Review** by the Grant Management (GM) team together with the EF team that owns the item. May include an interview, project rescoping or budget negotiation.
4. **Decision** by email. Most applications are reviewed within **3-6 weeks**. Selected projects agree a grant structure with **milestone-based payments**, then complete onboarding including identity verification and a formal grant letter.
5. **Execute** with a Grant Evaluator assigned for regular check-ins and milestone reviews.
6. **Complete** by publishing the results publicly in a report or post.

**Funding size:** ESP publishes no fixed award range. Per the ESP FAQ, "Grant funding is determined based on the scope and complexity of the proposal, unless otherwise specified in the posted Wishlist or RFP item. Where applicable, RFPs may include budget guidance estimates. The GM team will work with applicants to determine final grant amounts."

**Payment:** "Ethereum Foundation grants are paid on-chain in ETH by default", and recipients must be able to securely receive and manage ETH. Exceptions are considered only in limited cases where legal or operational constraints prevent receiving ETH.

ESP's own published allocation history: 136 projects / $26.9M (2021), 397 projects / $30.0M (2022), 498 projects / $61.1M (2023), 677 projects / $44.4M (2024).

You may apply to multiple Wishlist or RFP items, but each needs a separate application.

ESP was introduced on the Ethereum Foundation blog on 19 November 2019 — "Introducing the Ecosystem Support Program", published together with a call for applications directing applicants to esp.ethereum.foundation. That is the earliest ESP post on the blog and the date this record carries as `postedAt`.

**On the figures this record does not carry.** The allocation history above is historic disbursement, not a budget: ESP publishes no annual envelope, no round envelope — "There are no active grant rounds at this time" — and no per-grant range, and the FAQ quoted above declines to give one. The only ceiling ESP ever published belonged to the Small Grants track, "Small grants, capped at $30,000", and that track no longer exists: the page returns 404 and it is absent from the current sitemap, so it is not a current ceiling for anything. Budget guidance, where it exists at all, lives inside individual Wishlist or RFP items rather than at program level, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.
documents.summary: Rolling Ethereum Foundation grants for open-source public goods, applied for against a public Wishlist or a defined RFP.

operatingOrganizations.description: Stiftung Ethereum, a Swiss Stiftung (foundation) located at Zeughausgasse 7a, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. It operates ethereum.org, ethereum.foundation, esp.ethereum.foundation, devcon.org, devconnect.org and blog.ethereum.org. The Ecosystem Support Program is an ecosystem-development cluster within the Foundation, comprising the Grant Management and Funding Coordination teams.

ESP support is generally directed toward enabling builders rather than end-users.

Separate applications are required for each item. Grant recipients must complete identity verification, sign a formal grant letter, and be able to securely receive and manage on-chain ETH payments.

documents.title: Aave Grants
documents.description:
**This program has been sunset and is no longer accepting or reviewing new grant applications.**

Aave Grants DAO (AGD) was approved by the Aave DAO in May 2021 as a community grants program funded through the Aave DAO governance process — effectively a sub-DAO of the Aave DAO — with a group of Reviewers empowered to decide which proposals to fund. It funded contributors across eight categories: applications and integrations; code audits; committees & DAOs serving the Aave ecosystem; community (marketing and educational); developer tooling; events/hackathons/sponsorships; protocol development; and other. Early AGD grantees included Chaos Labs and TokenLogic, both of which later became Aave DAO service providers.

**Money.** AGD published one cumulative total for itself, in its September 2023 continuation proposal: "Since its inception in May 2021, AGD has awarded $4,852,753 across 249 grants", restated word for word in the Snapshot proposal that carried it. That is the last figure AGD ever published — it kept awarding into August 2024 but never posted the final overview it promised, and the January 2025 retrospective gives only "over 250 teams were supported" — so `allocated` here is committed-to-date as of September 2023, not a closing total.

The $500,000 ceiling is the founding proposal's own tiering: "Rapid grants: <$100k … Community grants: $100k-$500k … Contributors can also seek grants over $500k but they will not go through the committee. They will have to be posted on Aave's governance forum and approved through an on-chain vote." $500k is where this program ended and a DAO vote began. No later renewal restates or revokes the tiering, and aavegrants.org itself publishes no range.

**No `budget`, because AGD never had one envelope.** Aave funded it in five successive tranches, each sized in the proposal that granted it: $1M over two quarters at launch in May 2021; $2M for three months from December 2021; $3M per quarter for six months from May 2022; and $3.25M — $1.625M per quarter — for six months from January 2023. Any single one of them would understate the program and would sit oddly next to an allocated figure larger than it.

**Wind-down timeline:**
- August 2024 — "Update from Aave Grants: Winding Down AGD 1.0 and What's Next" announced that operations would be wound down and the team disbanded.
- January 2025 — "Reflecting on AGD's Journey and Next Steps" confirmed the wind-down, noting that as new service providers emerged their scope increasingly overlapped with AGD's broad funding mandate.
- February 2025 — an ARFC to return the remaining AGD treasury (321,768.10 GHO, 259,221.75 OP, 2,275.81 AAVE, 7,281.89 USDT, 6,738.05 USDC, 5,243.26 SAFE, 478.61 DAI) to the Aave DAO collectors passed Snapshot with 723.7K votes.
- 15 July 2026 — in response to a direct forum question asking whether the program was still active, Aave service provider TokenLogic replied: "You are correct that Aave Grants DAO has been sunset, and as part of that process, it is no longer accepting or reviewing new grant applications. As such, we wouldn't recommend preparing a submission through the AGD funding process."

The aavegrants.org site and its application form are still reachable and still carry the old rolling-applications copy, but they are stale: the site's news feed has not been updated since 2021 and the intake is not being reviewed. Prospective contributors are directed to engage the Aave DAO governance forum instead.

**Dating this record.** Aave published no announcement date for AGD, so `postedAt` is an archival bound rather than an announcement: the grants site was publicly visible by 11 May 2021, the first capture of aavegrants.org. The founding forum thread carries the corroborating update — "UPDATE – May 28, 2021: The proposal was ratified on-chain earlier this month, the grants DAO has been funded and we've started receiving applications."
documents.summary: Aave Grants DAO has been sunset and is no longer accepting or reviewing grant applications. The aavegrants.org site remains online but is stale; its treasury was returned to the Aave DAO in 2025.

Sunset in 2024-2025; its remaining treasury was returned to the Aave DAO collectors in February 2025. It is no longer accepting or reviewing grant applications.

documents.title: Lido Ecosystem Grants Organisation (LEGO)
documents.description:
LEGO (Lido Ecosystem Grants Organization) funds individuals, projects and initiatives that benefit the Lido protocol and the broader blockchain space — developers, crypto enthusiasts and community members with a plan to improve the ecosystem or raise awareness about Ethereum, proof-of-stake and DeFi.

**Grant classification — four tiers, all quoted in USD.** LEGO grants are "sorted into four different piles by expected size and impact". The tier determines who approves the grant, not when it may be submitted:

| Tier | Description | Approver | Grant amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sandgrain** | Contributions that are nice to have, yet not detrimental. Can be easily evaluated by a single person. | 1 member | up to 1,000 USD |
| **Pebble** | Non-critical, small things that are beneficial for Lido but not so trivial as to call a sand grain. | 2 members | up to 10,000 USD |
| **Boulder** | Big, important things that are imperative to be carried out by experts and thoroughly evaluated by core contributors. | Council vote | up to 100,000 USD |
| **Mountain** | Critical improvements to Lido with significant impact on its growth, security, operations, etc. | DAO vote | 100,000 USD + |

The Mountain tier has no published upper bound, so the 100,000 USD figure recorded as the maximum award is the top of the Boulder tier — the largest tier with a stated cap.

**Application process (rolling, no deadlines):**
1. **Contact** — reach the LEGO person responsible for your area of contribution (or any LEGO person, who will forward you) on **Telegram** to introduce yourself and your idea.
2. **Discuss grant terms** — hash out terms, timelines and deliverables in personal communication with the relevant LEGO member, who takes it through the LEGO approval process.
3. **Review** — the proposal is shared on the Lido research forum (research.lido.fi) and among LEGO committee members. On approval, communication channels are set up and the nominee receives funding.
4. **Present** — on completion, the creator presents the work to the LEGO committee.

Execution timelines vary by grant size and by how many committee members must take part.

**Committee:** LEGO has two segments. The **LEGO Council** is 8 partners, each responsible for a segment of Lido, each with a capacity of 15,000 LDO equivalent per quarter to fund sandgrain- and pebble-sized grants; only the Council votes on Boulders. **LEGO Nominees** are up to 20 individuals with a personal budget of 10,000 LDO equivalent per quarter (included in the total LEGO budget), managed by a vote of the LEGO Council. Any LEGO member can send a sandgrain, coordinate on pebbles and motion towards Boulders.

LEGO issues detailed quarterly reports on all granting activity at lego.lido.fi.

LEGO was introduced on the Lido research forum on 10 March 2021, in the topic "Project: Lido Ecosystem Grants Organization" — "a draft of the program for funding Lido ecosystem development with grants from the Lido Treasury".
documents.summary: Tiered rolling grants for work that benefits Lido and Ethereum staking, from small committee approvals up to DAO-vote grants.

documents.title: SSV Grants Program
documents.description:
The ssv.network Grants Program, **led by the SSV Foundation**, funds teams building services for the SSV Network ecosystem, with the intent of promoting and accelerating development and innovation by building on top of ssv.network. The program is presented publicly under the headline "$5M Grants Program" and is community-led.

**Grant categories:**
- **Open Grants** — supporting unique use cases for SSV across the ecosystem.
- **Strategic Partnerships** — partnerships to develop critical components like performance data, monitoring tools and integrations.
- **Performance and Metadata Providers** — reliable performance and metadata services for the SSV ecosystem.
- **Alerting & Monitoring Solutions** — tools for real-time network monitoring and alerting.
- **Alternative Client Implementations** — different client software to improve network resilience and diversification.
- **Staking Integrations** — partnering with major staking protocols to enhance ecosystem interoperability.
- **Developer Tools** — tools that assist developers building on the SSV network.
- **Bug Bounties** — run separately as a $1M program powered by Immunefi.
- **Micro Grants** — smaller grants for impactful contributions, often awarded retroactively, honouring those who significantly contributed to the community and the project in unforeseen ways. Anyone in the community can be awarded one or suggest a candidate.

**Process:** applications are reviewed on a rolling basis by the **Grants Committee**, which votes on approval and communicates the decision to the applicant. Accepted grant applications are published on the ssv.network forum. Milestone completion is then tracked closely together with the Grants Committee. All grantees must sign agreements with the SSV Foundation and complete **KYC/KYB**.

Grant sizes are negotiated per application rather than published as a range; the program's own showcase cites SSVScan (by DragonStake and Polkastats) as having received a **$300k** grant. Program contact: matthias@ssv.network.

The SSV Foundation published no announcement date, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the program's own public application page was publicly visible by 25 August 2022, its first capture. The SSV DAO forum proposal that created the program ("Eco-system Grant Program") was posted 12 April 2022.

All grantees must sign agreements with the SSV Foundation and complete KYC/KYB.

Successful applicants must sign an agreement with the SSV Foundation and complete KYC/KYB before funding, and milestone completion is tracked with the Grants Committee thereafter.

documents.title: Nouns DAO Small Grants
documents.description:
The Nouns DAO Small Grants Committee was created by **Nouns proposal 13**. It is run by a group of Nouners to be a "flexible pool of capital" that can be deployed when the project is time-sensitive, when the ask is too small for an official Nouns DAO proposal, or when retroactive funding is merited because the work is already done.

The committee's own scope statement is **"For projects needing 0.1-10Ξ"** — grants are denominated natively in ETH. The published grants ledger shows individual awards from 0.1 ETH up to about 27 ETH, with USD equivalents shown alongside for reference only.

**Two funding modes:**
- **Small Grant** — an upfront payment to fund a project.
- **Retroactive Funding** — a payment for work already completed.

**Requesting a grant:** open a post on the Nouns Discourse forum and prefix the title with "Small Grants: " for visibility. A committee member will then reach out to you, but you can also post the link to your Discourse post in the **#grants-and-retro-funding** channel in the Nouns Discord to get it on their radar. There are no deadlines.

**⚠️ Verification note (checked 2026-08-11):** the Discourse forum that this process depends on no longer exists — `discourse.nouns.wtf` does not resolve in DNS (and neither does `forum.nouns.wtf`), so every historical "Small Grants:" thread linked from the instructions is unreachable. The instructions page itself is live and unchanged, and the Nouns Discord invite still resolves, but the documented primary submission venue is dead and the committee's current operating status could not be established from any live page. Prospective applicants should confirm the current route in the Nouns Discord before relying on these instructions.

Proposal 13, "Retroactive Funding and Small Grants Pool", was proposed on 19 October 2021 by noun22.eth, which is the date this record carries as `postedAt`.
documents.summary: Rolling, community-run pool for small and time-sensitive Nouns projects, funded upfront or retroactively.

documents.title: MetaMask Grants Program
documents.description:
MetaMask Grants DAO is an employee-led, Consensys-funded DAO whose mission is to fund the development of high-value projects in the MetaMask ecosystem, supporting developers across the community to build on top of MetaMask while empowering Consensys employees to embrace web3 mechanisms.

**Structure — three parts:**
1. **Employee-Led DAO** — the body of the DAO, made up of full-time Consensys employees, with a stated intent to decentralize over time and add external contributors.
2. **Leadership Committee (mini-DAO)** — 7 individuals responsible for finding high-potential projects, creating governance proposals, updating external content, gathering feedback and queuing multisig transactions. If a member leaves Consensys, the remaining members may fill the seat by majority vote. Members are Dan Finlay, Aaron Davis (Kumavis), Taylor Monahan, Christian Montoya, Ryan Jones, Ian Wallis and Jordan Spence.
3. **Secure MultiSig** — a 2-of-3 Gnosis Safe controlled by Consensys that manages the token contract and treasury and signs disbursements.

**Two grant types:**
- **Leadership Committee Grants** — voted on exclusively by the Leadership Committee. Any Committee member may propose; proposals with at least **5 'yes' votes** at closing pass. Votes are open for **five days**.
- **Full DAO Grants** — voted on by the full DAO. Any Committee member may propose; proposals with more 'yes' than 'no' votes at closing pass. Votes are open for **ten days**.

Voting occurs on Activate, Consensys' proprietary platform built on top of Snapshot (the DAO's Snapshot space is `heart.mmgdao.eth`). Governance uses a non-transferable, fungible mainnet token that is mintable and burnable by the multisig and is "explicitly designed to never be exchanged for value"; all Consensys employees receive the same number of tokens, minted on joining and burned on departure.

**Intake:** external developers apply via a rolling application form. The DAO's Request for Proposals page states: "We are not currently running any RFP rounds, but our rolling grant applications remain open." There is no guaranteed review timeline — "We can't guarantee when we will review your request or that it will get approved, but know that our team will review the application pipeline as often as we can."

**No published range, and no envelope.** Nothing on the DAO's own site carries a dollar figure — not the FAQ's description of the two grant types, not the RFP page, not the grantee list. The closest it comes is a DAO objective stating that "More than 50% of the DAO's initial budget is allocated through tokenized proposal voting within the first three months of operation": the phrase "initial budget", without the number. Its Snapshot space holds sixteen proposals in total, of which three state an amount, and each states it as that grant's own size ($36,000, $35,000, $35,000) rather than as a range the program publishes. Consensys' launch announcement put the DAO's first-year funding at $2.4M, but that is the funder's press release rather than the program's own published budget, so this record carries no `fundingInfo` rather than promote it into one. The treasury cannot be read instead: it is described only as a 2-of-3 Gnosis Safe controlled by Consensys, with no address published anywhere on the site.

**On the open status:** the DAO's own RFP page still states that rolling grant applications remain open, which is what this record follows. Its Snapshot space has had no proposal since 22 December 2023, so the intake is open and the governance around it is quiet.

The DAO was launched on 27 October 2022, announced by Consensys as issuing grants to developers worldwide; metamaskgrants.org was first captured the same day.
documents.summary: Employee-led, Consensys-funded rolling grants for external developers building in the MetaMask ecosystem.

documents.title: Unichain Grants
documents.description:
The Uniswap Foundation funds work across the Uniswap Protocol and Unichain in five focus areas it publishes as: **Developers** (onboarding new developers to build on the Uniswap Protocol and supporting them through the development lifecycle), **Infrastructure** (new core infrastructure and growth strategies), **Governance** (empowering Uniswap governance to support protocol growth and sustain itself), **Research** (seeding DeFi research and its practical implementations), and **Security** (protecting the Protocol's users through investments into security). Its grants page groups the funded portfolio under Ecosystem, Research, Security and Governance.

**Payment currency and mechanics:** the Foundation's FAQ states that "Grant payments are currently made in fiat USD or USDC." During the Selection phase a team member works with the applicant to outline grant milestones, each tied to clear deliverables and to a portion of the overall payment; **grants typically have 2-5 milestones**, defined in the contract executed on approval. The initial payment is disbursed after KYC and contract signature, and subsequent payments on completion of each milestone. Every grantee is assigned a point person for 1-1 support and milestone check-ins.

Representative funded work includes the Uniswap Hook Incubator (Atrium Academy, 1,200+ applicants and 400+ developers onboarded), the OpenZeppelin v4 Hooks Library, the Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (Areta), v4 audits (OpenZeppelin, Trail of Bits, Cantina/Spearbit, ABDK, Certora), Unichain infrastructure and DeFi protocol onboarding support, the Protocol Grants Program (Auditless), Doppler (Whetstone), TLDR, and governance work with Agora, Blockful and Butter.

**⚠️ Intake state (checked 2026-08-11):** could not be confirmed. The Uniswap Foundation grants page at uniswapfoundation.org/grants is a funded-grants portfolio and impact page — it contains no application form, no apply call-to-action, and in fact no occurrence of the words "apply", "application", "submit" or "intake" anywhere in its markup; /grants/apply and /apply both return HTTP 404. The Foundation's FAQ describes an active application and selection process in the present tense, and the HubSpot form recorded on this program returns HTTP 200, but a HubSpot form shell returns 200 whether or not the round behind it is accepting. No published award range or deadline was found on any Uniswap Foundation page, so no funding figures are asserted here.

Unichain Developer Grants were announced by the Uniswap Foundation on 14 October 2024, in the post "Introducing Unichain Developer Grants".

**Why no figure is recorded.** The Foundation publishes no award range and no Unichain-earmarked envelope. The number that does exist is foundation-wide: the Uniswap Unleashed proposal, executed on-chain in March 2025, requested "an investment of $95.4M into the UF grants budget, and $25.1M to fund operations, for the next 2 years", with "projected grants budgets for 2025 and 2026 [of] $57.9M and $41.5M respectively" — across Ecosystem, Research, Security and Governance, and across both Uniswap protocol and Unichain work. Putting it on this record would assert an attribution the Foundation never made. The same proposal names the Unichain-specific programs (Developer Growth Programs, a Unichain Infrastructure Allocation, a Unichain DeFi Partner Allocation, Unigames) without sizing any of them; the per-program breakdown exists only inside an embedded chart image. The sibling $45M is liquidity incentives, not grants.

The one publication that might have carried a Unichain-earmarked figure — the original announcement on Mirror — is unrecoverable: Mirror migrated to Paragraph, the URL now serves that platform's own homepage and no capture of the post exists. The Foundation's blog post announcing the program, referenced above, is the live equivalent and carries no figure.

documents.title: Safe Ecosystem Foundation Grants
documents.description:
The Safe Ecosystem Foundation supports builders, researchers and communities advancing the adoption and security of smart account infrastructure. Its programs are governed by SafeDAO and powered by the SAFE token.

**What it funds (six areas):**
- **Protocol & Infrastructure** — core smart account improvements, module development, standards work (e.g. ERC-4337), and interoperability.
- **Security** — audits, formal verification, vulnerability research, and defensive tooling that hardens the Safe stack.
- **Developer Tooling & SDKs** — libraries, SDKs, APIs and integrations that make it easier to build on Safe.
- **Research** — academic and applied research on account abstraction, governance, key management and related topics.
- **Ecosystem Growth** — educational content, documentation, community events and adoption campaigns.
- **Applications** — products and services built on Safe that demonstrate novel use cases for smart accounts.

**Spontaneous Grants — the active rolling track.** "The Foundation accepts unsolicited grant proposals on a rolling basis. If you are building something that advances the Safe ecosystem and need financial support, we want to hear from you." Process:
1. Submit your proposal by email to grants@safefoundation.org.
2. Include: project description, scope & milestones, budget breakdown, team background, and expected impact.
3. The Foundation reviews proposals internally. **Expect an initial reply within 4 weeks.**
4. Approved grants are paid in milestones tied to deliverables.

No award range is published for the Spontaneous Grants track.

**Other initiatives (for context, not the rolling track):** the SafeDAO Grants Program Wave 1 is concluded (Aug 2023 - Jan 2024; 120 applications, 21 grants awarded, ~$500K deployed across Build, Growth, Research and Govern). SafeDAO OBRA, an outcomes-based allocation model of approximately $1.3M in stablecoins, is temporarily paused. The Safe smart account bug bounty is ongoing and separate, with rewards up to $1,000,000 for High severity, up to $50,000 for Medium and up to $10,000 for Low; six bounties worth $41,500 have been paid to date. Hackathon sponsorship is ongoing, with 100+ winner teams and $250K in prizes distributed.

The Foundation published no announcement post for the grants page, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the program was publicly visible by 11 March 2026, the first capture of the Foundation homepage that links /grants — the 8 January and 1 February 2026 captures carry no such link — and the grants page itself is first captured 19 April 2026.

**The missing number here is deliberate, and the same page proves it.** Spontaneous Grants is the only initiative on the Foundation's grants page with no figure attached — every other one is sized right there, as quoted above. The track runs the other way round: the applicant supplies the budget, in the "budget breakdown" the submission asks for, so there is no envelope for the Foundation to publish. Nor is one waiting in governance. SEP 54 (July 2025) established "a temporary funding pause on all resource allocation initiatives of SafeDAO", during which "the Foundation will assess and redesign the funding mechanisms based on learnings from previous approaches", and no replacement envelope has been published since; the forum has never discussed this track at all.

documents.title: Arbitrum Audit Program
documents.description:
The Arbitrum Audit Program (formally the Arbitrum Audit Subsidy Program) subsidised third-party smart contract audits for projects building in the Arbitrum ecosystem. It was funded by an ArbitrumDAO vote that requested 30,000,000 ARB from the treasury to be converted into a **$10,000,000 USD** audit budget plus $60,000 USD for the elected technical expert, with all unused ARB and USDC returned to the DAO at the end of the program. The subsidy is therefore USD-denominated even though the DAO appropriation and some auditor payments are made in ARB.

The program launched on 1 August 2025 and, per the DAO proposal, ran "an on-going open application for 1 year" or until funds were exhausted. As of 2026-08-11 the Tally intake form (tally.so/r/3xzEzv?program=aap) returns "This form is now closed — the form can't receive new submissions at this moment", so the application window has ended. The Arbitrum Foundation's grants index at arbitrum.foundation/grants still shows the program as "Active" with an "Apply now" button; that listing is stale relative to the live form.

Application process: an open standardised form collecting team information, project overview and evidence of product-market fit, stage of development and timeline to mainnet, audit scope (lines of code and languages), desired completion date, preferred auditor and requested audit budget. The Arbitrum Audit Committee — chaired by the Arbitrum Foundation, with Offchain Labs, a DAO-elected technical expert (Gustavo Grieco), and the ArbitrumDAO OpCo — reviewed applications on a rolling basis against technical maturity, team experience, likelihood of success, reasonable scope and Arbitrum-first commitment. Approved projects were then matched with one of the 12 approved audit firms (OpenZeppelin, Certora, Nethermind, Trail of Bits, Ackee Blockchain Security, Oak Security, Hexens, Decurity, Pashov Audit Group, OXORIO, Cyfrin, Guardian), and the project negotiated and paid a portion of the audit itself. Subsidies were paid only after the audit completed, disbursed by the Arbitrum Foundation directly to the auditor.

No per-project subsidy cap was ever published. The DAO proposal only used a planning assumption of "~$100k subsidy per project" to size the $10M budget; it is not a published maximum award.

Program results to date: Transparency Report #3 (covering 1 Feb – 30 Apr 2026) records 258 applications received across the first three quarters (81 in Q1, 69 in Q2, 108 in Q3), approximately $1.12 million committed for approved audits since launch, total commitments expected to reach roughly $2 million including audits in progress, and 297 vulnerabilities found (8 critical, 31 high) across 21,882 lines of code reviewed.
documents.summary: Closed as of 2026-08-11: the $10M USD Arbitrum audit-subsidy fund (financed by 30M ARB from the ArbitrumDAO treasury) ran a one-year open application window from 1 Aug 2025 and its Tally intake form now reports that it is closed.

operatingOrganizations.name: The Arbitrum Foundation
operatingOrganizations.description: The Arbitrum Foundation stewards the Arbitrum ecosystem and administers its grant and builder programs. It chairs the Arbitrum Audit Committee and disburses audit subsidies directly to approved auditors.

documents.eligibility: Applicants had to have auditable smart contract code (e.g. Solidity or Stylus) — infrastructure outside smart contracts was not subsidised. Eligible were early-stage projects yet to launch, projects with a significant code upgrade, projects already operational on Arbitrum that could demonstrate strong product-market fit or committed ecosystem alignment, and projects migrating from another blockchain to Arbitrum. Only new code, or code that had undergone significant modification, qualified. Projects must launch in the Arbitrum ecosystem (Arbitrum One, Nova, or their own Arbitrum chain). Audited code must remain exclusive to Arbitrum for a fixed period, written into the legal agreement; breaching exclusivity obligates the project to repay the full subsidy to the DAO via the Arbitrum Foundation and may lead to legal recourse and/or a DAO proposal banning the project from future DAO-funded initiatives. Having taken venture capital or other grants did not disqualify a team, but total funds raised was weighed by the committee. This is a subsidy, not full funding — the project pays a negotiated portion of the audit cost itself.
documents.additionalReferences: Program announcement: https://blog.arbitrum.foundation/arbitrums-10m-audit-program-is-live-apply-to-secure-your-smart-contracts/ | DAO proposal and full terms: https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/arbitrum-audit-program/28368 | Transparency Report #3 (Feb–Apr 2026): https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/arbitrum-audit-program-transparency-report-3/30976 | Audit-firm application process: https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/arbitrum-audit-program-audit-firms-application-process/29245 | Grants index: https://arbitrum.foundation/grants
documents.prerequisites: The standardised application collected: team information (names, background, notable investors); project information (overview and the problem solved, evidence or argument for product-market fit, stage of development and timeline to mainnet); audit coverage (scope of audit, lines of code and languages, desired completion date); and subsidy information (preferred auditor, optional, and the audit budget requested). Approved grantees additionally commit to publishing growth reports to the DAO at 2, 4 and 6 months after launching on Arbitrum, covering metrics such as TVL, protocol fees generated, integrations with other Arbitrum protocols and asset utilisation.

documents.title: Starknet Seed Grants
documents.description:
The Starknet Seed Grants Program provides up to $25,000 in non-dilutive funding to early-stage teams building in the Starknet ecosystem. Amounts are quoted in US dollars and paid out in STRK: the Starknet Foundation's own FAQ answers 'What currency are grants paid in?' with 'Seed Grants are paid out in STRK.'

Intake is continuous — 'you can apply for Seed Grants on an ongoing basis', with applications reviewed in rounds and no application deadlines. The Foundation targets a response in about one month (roughly four weeks).

Application process, in the Foundation's own five stages: (1) **Application** — apply via the grants submission form; all teams should present a clear plan detailing how the grant will be used within the next three months. (2) **Internal evaluation** — an internal committee assesses each application on potential impact, innovation, milestones, community engagement and track record, and embeddedness with the Starknet ecosystem. (3) **Results** — decisions communicated in approximately four weeks; rejected applicants are also notified. (4) **Onboarding** — after completing KYC/KYB and signing a grant agreement, funds are released. (5) **Post-grant check-in** — after three months the Foundation checks in with grantees to assess results, with grantees expected to share regular updates such as blog posts, videos and AMAs.

Applications are confidential and shared only with the Starknet Foundation and StarkWare teams. Repeat applications are permitted, and teams that have previously received StarkWare or Starknet Foundation funding may apply. Teams needing more than $25,000 are directed to the Growth Grants Program.

Seed Grants were announced by the Starknet Foundation on 6 May 2024, in the post "Announcing the Seed Grant Program".
documents.summary: Up to $25,000 (USD-denominated, paid in STRK) in non-dilutive funding for early-stage Starknet teams with an MVP or proof of concept; rolling intake with a decision in about four weeks.

operatingOrganizations.description: The Starknet Foundation runs the Starknet grants programs (Seed and Growth), supporting builders growing the Starknet ecosystem with non-dilutive funding paid in STRK plus non-financial guidance and follow-on introductions to its investor network. Grant applications are reviewed by an internal committee and shared only with the Starknet Foundation and StarkWare teams.

documents.eligibility: The Seed Grants Program aims to support early stage teams that have already developed a minimum viable product (MVP) or proof of concept but haven't yet gone to market. Publisher's stated criteria: actively involved in the Starknet community and/or participated in a Starknet hackathon, builder program, or other entry-level initiative; developed an MVP or proof of concept; plan on using or building upon existing Starknet tools and integrations, and planning to meaningfully contribute to the ecosystem in the future; building new applications in the ecosystem that have the potential to drive usage and build good user experiences for Starknet users. There are no restrictions on the types of products considered and no industry focus. Mature projects already live on Starknet with a core group of users are NOT eligible for Seed Grants and should apply to Growth Grants instead. KYC/KYB is legally required; any project unwilling to complete it is not eligible. The Starknet Foundation retains sole discretion over recipients and reserves the right to modify, amend or discontinue its grant programmes at any time without notice.

documents.title: Starknet Growth Grants
documents.description:
The Starknet Growth Grants Program provides non-dilutive funding to later-stage teams actively growing the Starknet ecosystem. The Foundation's grants overview publishes the band as **$25K to $1M STRK** — USD-denominated and paid in STRK — with the Growth Grants page itself stating 'Teams can receive up to $1M in funding'.

Growth Grants are organised into six categories, each with its own pre-filtered intake form: **Innovation Grants** (next-generation Starknet applications, infrastructure and protocols), **Ecosystem Integration Grants** (bridging Starknet with other networks and expanding interoperability), **Content & Creator Grants** (stories that educate and inspire Starknet users, or apps that make creators the owners of their own stories), **'The Next Billion'™ Grants** (intuitive, secure, accessible experiences that onboard the next billion users without compromising self-custody), **Bitcoin Builder Grant** (applications and infrastructure unlocking cross-chain possibilities between Starknet and Bitcoin), and **Other Grants**.

Intake is rolling with a target response of about one month. The process runs in six stages: (1) **Application** via the grants submission form, presenting a clear plan for using the grant within the next three months; (2) **Internal evaluation** by an internal committee against potential impact, innovation, milestones, community engagement, track record and embeddedness with the Starknet ecosystem; (3) **Interviews** — Growth applicants go through a rigorous interview process to understand their goals and requirements in the ecosystem; (4) **Results** communicated within approximately one month; (5) **Onboarding** after completing KYC and signing a grant agreement; (6) **Post-grant check-in** at three months, with grantees sharing regular updates such as blog posts, videos and AMAs.

The Starknet Foundation retains sole discretion over recipients and reserves the right to modify, amend or discontinue its grant programmes at any time without notice.

Growth Grants were announced by the Starknet Foundation on 17 September 2024 — "we are excited to announce the launch of Growth Grants! Growth Grants will provide up to $1M" — and the program page was first captured the same day.
documents.summary: Non-dilutive Starknet Growth Grants of $25K–$1M (USD-denominated, paid in STRK) for later-stage teams with a live, production-grade product and significant onchain traction; rolling intake, decision in about a month.

Teams are required to have a compelling and reliable product and to go through a rigorous review process including interviews. The grants overview additionally frames the stage bar as: later stage, production-grade product maturity, go-to-market required. Related Seed Grants FAQ guidance for stepping up to Growth: you have received a seed grant and performed exceptionally well, you have a product that is live, production grade and reliable, and your project fits within a Request for Proposals. KYC and a signed grant agreement are required before funds are released. Early-stage teams should apply to the Seed Grants Program instead.

documents.title: Starknet x Denarii Labs Accelerator
documents.description:
"Denarii Labs is partnering with the Starknet ecosystem to invest in and accelerate startups building on Ethereum's most powerful ZK-Rollup. From DeFi and gaming to AI agents and infrastructure — build with unlimited scale, low costs, and Ethereum-grade security." Denarii Labs describes itself as "a premier tokenomics accelerator and consulting agency backed by RedBeard Ventures".

Headline terms as published: Start Date Q3 2026 · Duration 12 Weeks · Format Remote · Investment $100K. From the FAQ: "Each project receives $100K in initial investment. Based on progress, projects may receive an additional $200K in follow-on funding. Terms are founder-friendly, structured as a SAFE or token warrant."

Program structure, four phases over 12 weeks: Weeks 1–2 Foundation & Mentoring (1-on-1 mentor matching, project assessment and gap analysis, token model framework selection, cohort kickoff); Weeks 3–6 Tokenomics Deep Dive (token supply and emission modeling, utility and demand driver design, distribution and vesting strategy, governance framework); Weeks 7–10 Execution & GTM (go-to-market strategy, community and narrative building, exchange listing prep, legal and compliance review); Weeks 11–12 Demo Day & Beyond (investor pitch preparation, Demo Day presentation, follow-on funding introductions, alumni network onboarding).

What participants get: "$100K investment from Denarii Labs; Direct access to the Starknet ecosystem; Weekly 1-on-1 sessions with tokenomics experts; Legal advisory for token models and compliance; Introductions to VCs, exchanges, and market makers; Post-program alumni network and continued advisory support."

Target projects, four buckets: DeFi & Financial Infrastructure (AMMs, DEXs and aggregators; lending, borrowing and yield protocols; perpetuals and structured products; stablecoin and synthetic asset platforms); Gaming & Onchain Worlds (fully onchain games using Dojo; in-game economies and asset systems; autonomous worlds and composable game logic; creator economy and digital collectibles); AI Agents & Verifiable Compute (verifiable AI inference and agent frameworks; provable ML model execution; tamper-proof data pipelines; autonomous onchain agents); Infrastructure & Tooling (Cairo developer tools and libraries; block explorers, indexers and APIs; bridges, oracles and cross-chain infra; SN Stack appchain tooling).

Admission and commitment, from the FAQ: teams need not already be building on Starknet ("We welcome teams exploring Starknet as well as those already building with Cairo") and need not know Cairo ("Cairo experience is helpful but not required"); the program is fully remote over 12 weeks with an expected "10–15 hours per week for mentor sessions, workshops, cohort calls, and independent work on tokenomics deliverables"; and "We typically accept 8–12 projects per cohort. We look for strong founding teams with a clear vision, a genuine need for tokenomics expertise, and a product with real traction or a compelling roadmap."

As of 2026-08-11 the page carries an "Applications Open" badge and live "Apply Now" buttons routing to the Airtable form; no application deadline is published.

The Starknet track was first announced in Denarii Labs' weekly newsletter of 5 March 2026 — "Join our current accelerator alongside Canton and Starknet". The 26 February 2026 issue does not mention Starknet and the accelerator index captured 17 January 2026 lists no Starknet track, which brackets the announcement to that date.

documents.title: World Foundation Spark Track Mini App Grant
documents.description:
The Spark Track is one of two active Mini App grant tracks in the World Foundation Grants program, which is funded from a pool of **50M WLD** — a token quantity, not a dollar figure. documents.title: Taiko Grants (2025 Grant Fund)
documents.description:
Taiko Grants is an ongoing grant fund announced on 19 March 2025 as 'Taiko Grant Cycle 3: $25M to Support Community Builders and Partners' — the Taiko 2025 Grant Fund, 'with a total of $25 million in funding'. The figure is quoted in US dollars only; the page nowhere denominates the fund in TAIKO tokens, so the record's currency is USD.

The fund supports developers, researchers and builders working on groundbreaking ideas in DeFi, AI, RWA, SocialFi, Gaming and beyond. Six grant tracks are published — DeFi (lending, borrowing, trading and other financial applications), AI (blockchain + artificial intelligence), RWA (tokenising and managing real-world assets), SocialFi (social networks with financial features), Gaming (gaming applications, NFT projects and metaverse experiences), and Other (projects leveraging Taiko's strengths such as Ethereum-equivalence, based design and permissionless proposing/proving) — and each is marked 'Applications open on an ongoing basis'.

As of 2026-08-11 the program page is live and unchanged in posture: 'The Grants Council will review applications on a rolling basis and reach out to applicants', the Airtable intake form returns HTTP 200, and no successor cycle or closure notice is published. The site footer reads '© 2026 Taiko Foundation'. No per-grant amount range is published anywhere on the page.

Program conditions: unless agreed otherwise, all smart contracts and frontend code must be open-sourced from the project's inception; projects involving dApps must choose Taiko as one of their first platforms (they may also deploy and integrate on other L1/L2/L3s); grantees and Taiko must establish a formal legal agreement detailing both parties' expectations and responsibilities; all grantees undergo KYC/KYB checks; and awardees may not disclose the grant — including the number of vested or received tokens — until Taiko has announced it. Grantees may hold grants from other projects concurrently provided all other requirements are met. Taiko also runs a separate ongoing initiative, Taiko Takeoff (takeoff.taiko.xyz).
documents.summary: Ongoing $25M USD Taiko grant fund (the 2025 Grant Fund / Grant Cycle 3) across six tracks — DeFi, AI, RWA, SocialFi, Gaming and Other — reviewed on a rolling basis by the Grants Council; still open and unsuperseded as of 2026-08-11.

documents.eligibility: Open to developers, researchers and builders working on groundbreaking ideas in DeFi, AI, RWA, SocialFi, Gaming, and beyond. 'Projects involving dApps must choose Taiko as one of their first platforms, but they can also deploy and integrate on other L1/L2/L3s.' Taiko looks favourably on Taiko-tailored projects, i.e. those that truly take advantage of Taiko's strengths and design decisions such as Ethereum-equivalence, based design, and permissionless proposing/proving. All grantees must undergo KYC/KYB checks and sign a formal legal agreement with Taiko. Grantees may apply for and hold grants from other projects, given all other requirements are met. documents.title: Base Ecosystem Fund
documents.description:
"Base Ecosystem Fund is the strategic investment arm of Base. In partnership with Coinbase Ventures, we invest in pre-seed and seed stage startups that choose Base as their home. Our approach is borderless and uncompromisingly team-centric, focusing on accelerating the elite builders on Base." The fund positions itself as "Pairing early-stage capital with deep ecosystem alignment to ensure the best teams have the resources to achieve venture-scale growth from day one."

Mission: "to catalyze the Base economy by backing ambitious founders focused on delivering venture scale outcomes." Investment strategy: "We invest in the world's top talent building the next generation of enduring and high-performance onchain primitives & businesses that drive real economic activity and define the onchain future."

What portfolio companies get, in three published buckets: White Glove Support — "Hands-on support from our ecosystem team to unlock partner integrations and amplify distribution"; Exclusive Perks — "Unlock credits from our partners including AWS, Azure, Alchemy, Spindl ad credits and more"; and Coinbase Access — "Get priority access to Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Business, and Coinbase Onramp API".

The Ecosystem Fund is one rung of a published six-stage support ladder: (01) Idea — Base Batches, "Base's in-house Accelerator program"; (02) Pre-seed & Seed — Ecosystem Fund; (03) Growth — Coinbase Ventures; (04) Private Fundraise — Echo; (05) Public Token Sale — Sonar by Echo; (06) Listing — Coinbase. Teams at idea stage are therefore routed to Base Batches rather than to this fund.

Portfolio companies named on the page: Aerodrome, Avantis, Limitless, A0X, B3, BANKR, Berry, Blockrun, Boardwalk, Charms, Credit Coop, Crown, Ethos, Exactly Protocol, Flyra, Giza, Glider, HeyElsa, Jia, Kash, Kontigo, LiveFrame, Nuzo, Offramp, Onboard, OpenCover, Paragraph, Pred, Remix, Sapien, Senpi, Sport.Fun, Tailgate, Tenor, Truflation, Veil, ViFi, Wrapped CBDC and Zynk, filterable by Trading, Payments, AI Agents and Other.

Application is a multi-step form at base.org/ecosystem-fund/apply with sections for Company, Team, Idea, Funding and Why Base; the first step asks for Company Name, "What are you building?", Website URL and X URL. No fund size, check size, instrument, ownership target, deadline or decision timeline is published.

The fund was announced on 23 February 2023, in Coinbase's Base launch post: "We're also announcing the Base Ecosystem Fund, which invests in and supports early stage projects building on Base that meet our investment criteria. If you're interested, please fill out the form here." That is the entire announcement — it names no fund size, no check size and no target project count.

**Nothing about the money is published — and Base publishes it for its neighbouring programs.** The fund page carries no fund size, check size, instrument, ownership target or decision timeline; the launch announcement quoted above named none; and the first-cohort post quantifies only demand ("We received over 800 applications for our Base Ecosystem Fund") with no per-deal amounts for any of the six investments. Base's own funding documentation does publish ranges one rung either side — Builder Rewards "distributes 2 ETH weekly", Builder Grants a "Grant Range: 1-5 ETH" — and lists the Ecosystem Fund with no figure at all. There is no earlier version to fall back on either: the fund page has never been archived. The absence is the fund's own posture, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.

documents.title: Polymarket Builders Program
documents.description:
The Polymarket Builders Program offers **over $2.5M in grants** for developers building apps, tools and experiments on top of Polymarket. Amounts are quoted only in US dollars on the program page; the associated weekly builder rewards are explicitly paid in USDC, which Polymarket settles in.

Grants: 'Grants are distributed to the best teams based on product innovation and traction.' Polymarket names the kinds of projects it wants — integrating Polymarket markets inside your app; distributing to a specific vertical or geography; building a pro trading terminal with advanced orders; empowering users with new analytics, portfolio managers and AI decisions; launching a new type of media powered by prediction markets; or creating DeFi primitives such as lending and vaults. A 'Request for Builders' page (builders.polymarket.com/rfb) publishes the team's own idea list — explicitly framed as a prompt rather than a constraint. Support includes technical support and amplification on Polymarket's social channels.

Weekly rewards: separately from grants, 'the most active builders earn extra weekly rewards based on volume'. Polymarket describes it as a weekly USDC rewards program launched to bootstrap Builder Codes integrations, paid on integration volume. Each reward epoch runs from Sunday 00:00 UTC to Saturday 23:59 UTC. Builder Codes are unique credentials that let builders attribute orders to their builder profile and grant access to the Polymarket Relayer API; volume is credited for every matched trade attributed to the builder account and appears on the public Builder Leaderboard within about 24 hours. No per-epoch pool size or payout formula is published. As of 2026-08-11 the leaderboard's top integration shows ~$40.04M of 1-month volume.

Joining is permissionless — 'Polymarket DeFi protocol is free and permissionless to use and access. Just start building to be part of the program!' — and there is no deadline. The grant application is an in-page form on builders.polymarket.com.

Polymarket published no announcement post for the program, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the Builders Program site was publicly visible by 2 November 2025, its first capture, which is also the start of the weekly builder-rewards program it runs alongside.
documents.summary: Rolling Polymarket Builders Program: over $2.5M USD in grants for apps, tools and experiments built on Polymarket, awarded on product innovation and traction, plus a weekly USDC rewards program paid on Builder Codes integration volume in Sunday-to-Saturday UTC epochs.

operatingOrganizations.name: Polymarket
operatingOrganizations.description: Polymarket is a prediction-market protocol and platform. Its website footer identifies Adventure One QSS Inc. as the operating company, and states that Polymarket operates globally through separate legal entities — the US platform is operated by QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US, a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market, while the international platform is not CFTC-regulated and operates independently. Polymarket runs the Builders Program for developers building apps, tools and experiments on top of the protocol.

documents.eligibility: Participation is permissionless: 'Polymarket DeFi protocol is free and permissionless to use and access. Just start building to be part of the program!' Grants are then distributed to the best teams based on product innovation and traction. To appear on the builder leaderboard and earn weekly volume-based rewards you must integrate Builder Codes and get in touch with the team for verification. Token policy, in the publisher's own words: 'Builders must inform the team ahead of any potential token launch. Tokens launched without public communication or transparency, or solely for short-term extraction or pump-and-dump purposes, will result in badge removal. Projects with contract addresses in their bio or constant shilling are not welcome.' A Code of Conduct is published at builders.polymarket.com/code-of-conduct.

documents.title: Ethereum Foundation Bug Bounty Program
documents.description:
The Ethereum Foundation's rolling bug bounty for consensus and execution-layer specs, the major client implementations (Geth, Reth, Nethermind, Erigon, Besu, Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Lodestar, Grandine), Solidity and Vyper, and the deposit contract.

The ethereum.org bug bounty page confirms the program is 'Open for submissions' with no end date and severity tiers reaching $1,000,000 for a critical finding, submitted through the Foundation's own report form.

The program was introduced publicly on 18 December 2014, in the Foundation's blog post "A call to all the bug bounty hunters out there…", which opened bounties on the protocols, the Go implementation and the network code; a follow-up in March 2015 confirms it running from around that time.
documents.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's rolling protocol and client bug bounty, paying up to $1,000,000 for a critical finding.
documents.eligibility: Awards cannot be issued to individuals on sanctions lists or resident in countries on sanctions lists. Proof of identity is required by local law, and the reporter is responsible for all taxes. Employees, contractors, service providers or grantees of the Ethereum Foundation, and members of client teams in scope, may accrue leaderboard points only and receive no monetary reward during the relationship and for 90 days after it ends. Determinations of eligibility and award are at the sole discretion of the Ethereum Foundation bug bounty panel.

fundingDetails.severityScheme: Ethereum Foundation bug bounty vulnerability severity qualifications (validator-slashing / network-split / network-liveness thresholds)

documents.additionalReferences: In scope: protocol soundness (consensus model, wire and p2p protocols, proof of stake), the Consensus Layer and Execution Layer specifications, execution-layer clients (Besu, Erigon, Geth, Nethermind, Reth) and consensus-layer clients (Lighthouse, Lodestar, Nimbus, Teku, Prysm, Grandine), the Solidity and Vyper compilers, the Beacon Chain deposit contract specification and source, and the dependencies C-KZG-4844 and Go-KZG-4844. Out of scope: infrastructure such as webpages, DNS and email; ERC-20 contract bugs; ENS bugs; issues requiring a publicly exposed API such as JSON-RPC or the Beacon API; the Engine API, which is treated as trusted; typographical errors; tests; high-effort single-peer DoS; publicly known issues; and anything without direct impact on Ethereum mainnet. Programme rules and scope: https://ethereum.org/bug-bounty/ (bounty.ethereum.org redirects here). Submission form: https://bbp-form.ethereum.org/ . A public leaderboard of past reporters is published on the rules page. Program announcement (18 December 2014): https://blog.ethereum.org/2014/12/18/call-bug-bounty-hunters.
documents.prerequisites: A reproducible proof of concept is mandatory: either a Kurtosis-based PoC that spins up a local devnet, or a state test (EVM/goevmlab); plain unit tests are not accepted. For Solidity/Vyper compiler bugs a Kurtosis or state test is not required, but the triggering source, the exact affected compiler versions, a comparison against a working version and step-by-step reproduction are. A burn in ETH is required to submit a report as an anti-spam measure, and there are no refunds. Reports without a PoC, already submitted by another reporter, already known to spec or client maintainers, or publicly disclosed beforehand, are ineligible.

documents.title: The Graph Grants Program
documents.description:
**⚠️ Applications are paused.** On 6 July 2026 The Graph Foundation announced on its official forum: "The Graph Foundation is pausing applications to the Grants Program. Over the years, the Grants Program has supported grantees across the ecosystem with millions of dollars in funding. In recent months, we made the decision to pause the Grants Program to reassess our ecosystem strategic priorities." No reopening date has been announced.

Note that the public grants page at thegraph.com/grants and its Typeform application link were both still reachable when checked on 2026-08-11 and had not been updated to reflect the pause, so page liveness alone is not evidence that intake is open.

**Program as documented.** The Graph grants program is a gateway for contributing to web3, awarding grants for protocol, tooling, subgraph and dapp development, and growth initiatives, distributed from the community treasury. It is overseen by **The Graph Foundation and The Graph Council**, with support from community domain experts and core contributors. Grants go to individuals, projects and initiatives that are open source and contribute to the growth of The Graph ecosystem — "You don't have to be technical to receive a grant!"

**Four categories:**
- **Protocol** — advance The Graph Network with R&D on smart contracts, network operations, Graph Node, cryptography and other core development.
- **Tooling** — subgraph and Indexer tooling to improve developer experience, expand features, help users engage with the network and simplify network operations.
- **Data Services** — create and use subgraphs and Substreams to build new data services, dapps and dashboards.
- **Community** — grow the network, subgraph usage and web3 knowledge through education, content, events and developer support.

Grants have been awarded in numbered waves; the public grantee directory lists 100 grantees. The separate RFP track shows "There are no open RFPs at this time".

**Scale:** The Graph Foundation's 2025 Annual Grants Report states lifetime grant funding exceeding **$16.8M**. In 2025 the program funded five R&D teams delivering Horizon, advanced the Token API to production readiness, integrated AI-native tooling via Subgraph MCP, and expanded multi-chain coverage.

The program was announced on 11 December 2020, alongside the inaugural Graph Council: "Announcing The Graph Council members and The Graph Grants Program to support ecosystem development", with the first grants estimated for Q1 2021.
documents.summary: The Graph Foundation paused applications to the Grants Program on 6 July 2026 to reassess ecosystem strategic priorities. Lifetime grant funding exceeds $16.8M. The thegraph.com/grants page and its Typeform still load but are not accepting new applications.

operatingOrganizations.name: The Graph Foundation
operatingOrganizations.description: Steward of The Graph's community treasury and operator of The Graph Grants Program, which it oversees jointly with The Graph Council, supported by community domain experts and core contributors. It publishes annual grants reports; lifetime grant funding exceeds $16.8M. It paused applications to the Grants Program on 6 July 2026 to reassess ecosystem strategic priorities.

documents.eligibility: Anyone may apply — no invitation or pre-selection.

documents.title: Rocket Pool GMC Grants — Round 40
documents.description:
Round 40 of the Rocket Pool Grants Management Committee (GMC) grants track. Grants are for applicants who wish to **carry out the work themselves** — as distinct from bounties, which are open-ended goals that could be met by anyone, including parties other than the proposer.

**Round 40 schedule (from the call for applications):**
- Application Period: **August 7 - September 7, 2026**
- Scoring Deadline: **September 22, 2026**
- Final Voting Amendments, Discussion and Finalization: **September 23 - September 26, 2026**
- Award Announcement: **September 27, 2026**

**Submission mechanics:** applications are posted as **replies in the round's own forum thread** on the Rocket Pool DAO Discourse, using the published grant application template. "Only those grant applications that are posted in this thread and timestamped by September 7, 2026 at 23:59 (11:59 PM) UTC will be considered. Any grants posted after that deadline will be carried over to the next award period." Questions and discussion of submitted applications go in a separate community discussion thread, not the application thread.

**GMC goals.** Grants, bounties and retrospective awards should make it easier and/or more attractive to do one or more of the following: become a node operator; operate a node, mint rETH; hold or use rETH; improve the quality of life for the protocol and its community.

**Grants scoring rubric.** When evaluating grant applications the GMC considers: (1) if the application is successful, to what extent does it further the GMC goals; (2) to what extent can the application be feasibly carried out by the person(s) proposed to complete it; (3) if the application is successful, how large is the benefit to the protocol relative to the size of the proposed costs.

**Award sizing.** The GMC publishes no per-grant cap. Applicants state their own ask, and the application template asks it **in US dollars**: "How much USD $ and over what period of time is the applicant requesting?" Payment is made from the committee's RPL treasury — the July 2026 treasury report notes that month's payments were made at an RPL price of $1.77, and the committee separately executes RPL-to-USDC swaps to settle awards. The GMC can only send grants directly to a recipient address and cannot accept invoices.

**Microgrants.** Following a GMC vote, a microgrant framework was introduced (announced May 2026) in response to treasury constraints. Microgrants use the existing GMC grant system with no process changes and no separate application type — contributors submit standard applications and the GMC may choose to award a microgrant. Microgrants "will typically fall into one of the following ranges: 10 RPL, 50 RPL, 100 RPL". They can be used for both new submissions and retrospective recognition, are intended as partial recognition given current constraints, may be revisited if treasury conditions improve, and there is no limit on how many a contributor can receive.

Because the applicant's ask is denominated in USD while microgrant tiers are quoted natively in RPL, and neither constitutes a published program-wide award range, no minAward/maxAward or currency is asserted on this record.

Round 40 is confirmed as the current round as of 2026-08-11: it is the most recent call for applications in the Grants / Bounties category, posted 2026-08-08, and no later round has superseded it.

The governing RPIP sets no per-grant cap and no per-round pool either; its only budget statement points upstream, to the share of the protocol-level budget set aside for grants and bounties together. Nothing at this record's level has ever been published as a number, which is why it carries no `fundingInfo`.

documents.title: Rocket Pool GMC Retrospective Awards — Round 40
documents.description:
Round 40 of the Rocket Pool Grants Management Committee (GMC) **retrospective awards** track — recognition for work that has already been completed, as opposed to the grants track, which funds work an applicant proposes to carry out. The round covers Rocket Pool's **July 7, 2026 - September 7, 2026 retrospective awards**.

**Round 40 schedule (identical to the grants track):**
- Application Period: **August 7 - September 7, 2026**
- Scoring Deadline: **September 22, 2026**
- Final Voting Amendments, Discussion and Finalization: **September 23 - September 26, 2026**
- Award Announcement: **September 27, 2026**

**Submission mechanics:** applications are posted as **replies in the round's own retrospective-applications forum thread** on the Rocket Pool DAO Discourse, using the published retrospective award template. "Only those retrospective award applications that are posted in this thread and timestamped by September 7, 2026 at 23:59 (11:59 PM) UTC will be considered. Any retrospective award applications posted after that deadline will be carried over to the next award period." Questions and discussion of submitted applications go in a separate community discussion thread.

**GMC goals.** Grants, bounties and retrospective awards should make it easier and/or more attractive to do one or more of the following: become a node operator; operate a node, mint rETH; hold or use rETH; improve the quality of life for the protocol and its community.

**Retrospective award rubric — a single criterion:** "To what extent did the proposed and completed project further the GMC goals?" With the note: if the project is ongoing, the retrospective award is given for work completed prior to the current award period, and any future awards for the same project are expected to compete in the Grants category as a separate application. This is a narrower rubric than the three-part grants rubric, which also weighs feasibility and cost-benefit — feasibility is moot for work already delivered.

**Award sizing.** No per-award cap is published. The template asks the applicant to state the ask **in US dollars**: "How much USD $ is the applicant requesting be awarded to the recipient?" Awards are settled from the committee's RPL treasury, which receives 16,265.35 RPL every 28 days under RPIP-81, shared across the grants, bounty and retrospective tracks. The microgrant framework introduced in May 2026 applies to this track too — microgrants "can be used for both new submissions and retrospective recognition" and typically fall into 10 RPL, 50 RPL or 100 RPL tiers. Because the ask is denominated in USD while microgrant tiers are quoted natively in RPL, and neither is a published program-wide award range, no minAward/maxAward or currency is asserted on this record.

Round 40 is confirmed as the current round as of 2026-08-11: it is the most recent call for retrospective applications in the Grants / Bounties category, posted 2026-08-08.

The only ceiling that governs this track is a relative one — RPIP-15 provides that "in any given award period, no more than 50% of the awarded RPL SHALL go to retroactive awards" — and the round's total awarded amount is never published in advance, so that share cannot be resolved into a figure. Round 38, the most recent published results, recorded no retrospective applications at all. This record therefore carries no `fundingInfo`.

documents.title: Mantle EcoFund
documents.description:
The Mantle EcoFund is Mantle's ecosystem investment vehicle for early-stage projects seeking a long-term partnership with Mantle Network. It was established by Mantle governance proposal MIP-24, posted to the Mantle forum on 26 February 2023, which 'authorized the establishment of a US$100 million Mantle EcoFund capitalised by the Mantle Treasury'; capital is drawn down in tranches through governance-approved capital calls denominated in USDC (a first call of US$10 million, then a second call of US$30 million authorised by MIP-29 in February 2024, which also expanded the fund's investment mandate). Mantle's own site currently describes the EcoFund as having 'a $200M catalyzed capital pool… accessing top-tier deal flow through 20 leading VCs like Polychain and Dragonfly' — that larger figure is the catalysed pool including co-investor capital, not the DAO-authorised fund size. Mirana Ventures plays a strategic role supporting the fund.

This is investment and partnership support rather than a fixed grant cheque. Investment criteria, in Mantle's words, look for projects that are early stage; are seeking a long-term partnership with Mantle; can attract capital from venture firms and allocators; and synergize with other Mantle Ecosystem partners.

Support provided is split into two tiers. Exclusively for EcoFund portfolio companies: the EcoFund 'EF' tag, and deal-structuring and fundraising support. Prioritized for them (and also provided to top-performing applications on Mantle generally): Mantle co-promotion on media, social and events; enhanced delegated voting; listing recommendations to partnered exchanges; liquidity support via the Economics Committee program; and direct access and regular catch-ups with the Mantle Growth team.

Intake is by email rather than a public form: the EcoFund page's 'Contact Us' resolves to ecofund@mantle.xyz, with the suggested subject line 'Join Mantle EcoFund as a Strategic Venture Partner'. The page lists 40+ portfolio companies across DeFi, gaming, Bitcoin infrastructure, RWA and AI, many tagged 'Live'. No closing date is published. Historic selectivity disclosed in governance: between 1 September 2023 and 15 January 2024 the EcoFund team reviewed 252 projects, took 58 (23%) into deeper due diligence, and invested in 10 (3.9%).
documents.summary: Rolling Mantle EcoFund: a US$100M DAO-authorised ecosystem investment fund (described by Mantle as a $200M catalysed capital pool with 20 co-investing VCs) offering partnership, fundraising and growth support to early-stage projects; intake is by email to ecofund@mantle.xyz.

documents.title: ArbiFuel (Gas Fee Sponsorship Program)
documents.description:
ArbiFuel is the Arbitrum Foundation's Gas Fee Sponsorship Program, launched 29 May 2025, to help early-stage teams ship faster, test freely and onboard users without worrying about gas costs. Selected projects get sponsorship of **up to 1,000,000 free transactions in their first year** following the start of the gas sponsorship, **capped at $10,000 USD in credits per team**. The cap is quoted in US dollars and is delivered as sponsorship credit rather than a cash grant.

Sponsorship is initially powered by Pimlico's ERC-20 Paymasters, with plans to expand to other paymasters based on project needs, so end users do not need ETH to transact in the sponsored application. The program is framed around Arbitrum's push toward native smart-account support following upgrades such as Pectra and EIP-7702.

As of 2026-08-11 the Arbitrum Foundation's grants index lists ArbiFuel as Active, 'Managed by The Arbitrum Foundation', with a live 'Apply now' button; the Airtable intake form returns HTTP 200. No deadline or window is published — intake is rolling.

ArbiFuel also asks teams to educate their communities about being on Arbitrum and the availability of gasless transactions; the Foundation states that community education and awareness can strengthen an application.
documents.summary: Rolling Arbitrum gas-fee sponsorship: up to 1,000,000 sponsored transactions in a team's first year, capped at $10,000 USD in credits per team, delivered via Pimlico ERC-20 Paymasters. Intake verified live on 2026-08-11.

operatingOrganizations.name: The Arbitrum Foundation
operatingOrganizations.description: The Arbitrum Foundation stewards the Arbitrum ecosystem and administers its grant and builder programs, including ArbiFuel, the Arbitrum Audit Program and the Trailblazer grant programs.

documents.eligibility: In the Foundation's own words, 'The Arbitrum Foundation welcomes the following to apply for gas sponsorship under ArbiFuel: Early-stage developers working on simplified UX apps; Wallet providers and stablecoin-related products; Teams exploring payment-related applications.' The program is aimed at teams exploring smart wallets, onboarding UX or payment-related applications on Arbitrum. Applicants are also encouraged to actively educate their communities about their presence on Arbitrum and about the opportunity to benefit from gasless transactions on Arbitrum protocols — the Foundation states that community education and awareness can strengthen an applicant's chances of receiving gas sponsorship.
