documents.title: Arbitrum Gaming Ventures (AGV)
documents.description:
**Wound down by DAO vote.** On 24 June 2026 a proposal was posted to the Arbitrum forum seeking "DAO approval for AGV to cease forward investment activity and return surplus capital to the DAO treasury for redeployment", recording that "AGV has already ceased making new investments; its remaining activities will be limited to portfolio management, information transfer, and the orderly completion of the wind-down process." It passed, and on 7 July 2026 the Arbitrum Foundation confirmed it had returned the 86.18M ARB it held on AGV's behalf to the DAO treasury — part of roughly 143.7M ARB in total, the balance being what remained inside AGV. The expression-of-interest form below was still reachable when this record was written on 2026-08-11, and the Foundation's grants index still listed the program, but new investment has ended; the 225M ARB below is what the DAO backed the program with, not what is left to deploy.

Arbitrum Gaming Ventures (AGV) is the ArbitrumDAO's gaming and consumer venture initiative — the renamed successor to the Gaming Catalyst Program (GCP). The old GCP domain thegamingcatalyst.com now redirects to arbitrumgamingventures.com, confirming the rebrand. The Arbitrum Foundation states AGV is 'Backed by 225M ARB from the ArbitrumDAO'; the figure is a native token quantity, so this record's currency is ARB rather than USD.

AGV describes itself as investing in 'teams creating exceptional experiences at the intersection of blockchain gaming, entertainment, and culture'. It 'deploys investment and grant funding to proven publishers and rising indies, using flexible deal structures such as grants, co-investments, equity, or token models to meet entrepreneurs where they are'. Support extends beyond capital to user-acquisition and scaling capital, strategic partnerships and go-to-market help, for teams ranging from AAA studios to indie creators. Its published thesis pillars are Funding Breakthroughs (projects with breakout potential, retentive user experiences and novel distribution strategies), Arbitrum Everywhere, and Bet on Talent, Big or Small.

Governance and operations: AGV is run by an operating team (Partners, a General Manager, a Venture Associate, a Grants Program Lead, a General Counsel and a Content and Communications Lead) overseen by an elected AGV Council including an Investment Committee member and an Arbitrum Foundation observer. Council seats run on a calendar-year term with nominations in October, voting in November and transition in December. The program's official start date was 1 January 2025. Its H2 2025 transparency report records the thesis broadening beyond gaming into gamified consumer platforms, prediction markets and other onchain-native experiences, and a more capital-disciplined deployment posture given ARB price volatility.

Disclosed portfolio companies include Giant, Golden Tides, Forkast, The Lost Glitches, Coverd, Hyve Labs, Wildcard, T-Rex, Forge.gg, Jin Anomaly, XAI and Thousands.

Intake: AGV runs a standing expression of interest at arbitrumgamingventures.com/apply — 'If you are working on the next big thing in gaming, entertainment, or consumer, we want to hear from you. Apply to become a part of the AGV portfolio and bring your vision to life on Arbitrum.' There is no published deadline and no per-deal size is disclosed. The Arbitrum Foundation's grants index lists AGV as Active with a 'Submit Interest' button, 'Managed by The ArbitrumDAO'.

AGV was publicly launched under this name on 8 May 2025, in a press release revealing its first $10M investment cohort; arbitrumgamingventures.com was first captured five days later.
documents.summary: ArbitrumDAO's gaming, entertainment and consumer venture arm (formerly the Gaming Catalyst Program), backed by 225M ARB. The DAO voted it wound down in mid-2026: AGV has ceased new investment and ~143.7M ARB is being returned to the treasury, with remaining activity limited to portfolio management and an orderly close.

documents.title: ProPGF Batch 2 - Pods Track
documents.description:
The Pods Track is a coordination track designed to help Filecoin teams organize around clear user outcomes and move faster toward product–market fit (PMF).

Instead of funding isolated projects, the Pods Track supports small, focused pods (cross-functional where possible) that are accountable for shipping a defined scope, validating user needs, and contributing to Filecoin’s 2026 ecosystem goals. Pods are expected to operate like product teams: aligning on a problem, testing assumptions, delivering milestones, and reporting progress through measurable adoption and performance metrics.

**What was allocated, and how that number was arrived at.** No Pods Track pool was ever published: the ProPGF blog announces and reports only the Batch 2 General Track — a $4M round that allocated $3,220,200 across 16 projects — and the Pods Track has no announcement, no results post and no published total anywhere. What the program does publish is per-pod, in its own financials ledger: Filecoin Onchain Cloud 466,000, the Large Data Onboarding Pod 147,630, and the Web2 Object Storage Pod 267,344. The 880,974 USD on this record is those three figures summed from that ledger and nothing else — a sum of the program's own per-grant allocations, not a funder-published program total, and not a budget. It is Pods-Track-only and deliberately excludes the General Track, which is a separate record with its own budget and its own allocation. Two of the three grants settle in USDC and the third's milestones are dollar-denominated, which is what denominates the record.

documents.eligibility: Not open to all applicants — the program invites or pre-selects participants.

documents.title: Filecoin ProPGF Batch 3
documents.description:
Filecoin ProPGF Batch 3 is a $2M milestone-based funding program designed to support critical ecosystem work that strengthens the Filecoin network and advances long-term ecosystem priorities. The standard scope of submitted projects should be within 3 to 6 month term. 

Batch 3 supports two primary categories of work:
- Core Infrastructure Maintenance: Funding for the maintenance and continued improvement of core infrastructure the Filecoin network depends on, including implementations, critical libraries, dependencies, indexing systems, retrieval infrastructure, and essential services that support network reliability and performance.
- RFP Responses: Funding for projects responding to specific Requests for Proposals (RFPs) published on [filpgf.io](https://filpgf.io/blog/propgf-batch-3-call-for-builders/) and [filecoin.io](https://www.filecoin.io/blog). These RFPs focus on support and innovation work aligned with operational and ecosystem priorities identified by Pods and ecosystem stakeholders.

Applicants are encouraged to review [The Filecoin Network Strategy](https://www.filecoin.io/blog/the-2026-filecoin-network-strategy) to help align proposals with broader ecosystem growth goals.
documents.eligibility: Not open to all applicants — the program invites or pre-selects participants.
documents.additionalReferences: Call for builders: https://filpgf.io/blog/propgf-batch-3-call-for-builders/ · Network strategy: https://www.filecoin.io/blog/the-2026-filecoin-network-strategy

documents.title: Filecoin ProPGF Batch 2
documents.description:
Filecoin ProPGF Batch 2 is a $4M milestone-based funding program designed to accelerate innovation and strengthen the Filecoin ecosystem.

The program supports projects that make Filecoin more useful, resilient, and impactful — spanning infrastructure, research, governance, and user experience. It provides milestone-based grants to teams that directly contribute to the network’s growth, sustainability, and adoption.

The General Track funds a broad range of initiatives, including but not limited to:

1. Tooling & Developer Ecosystem – SDKs, APIs, infrastructure, and developer tools that improve the Filecoin developer experience.

2. Research – Technical, economic, or design research that advances the Filecoin protocol or ecosystem.

3. Customer Success – Initiatives that strengthen onboarding, documentation, and adoption across the ecosystem.

4. Governance – Mechanisms, tools, or frameworks that enhance transparency and collective decision-making.

5. End-User UX – Interfaces, integrations, and applications that make Filecoin more intuitive for everyday users.
documents.summary: Filecoin ProPGF Batch 2 is a $4M milestone-based funding program designed to accelerate innovation.
documents.eligibility: Not open to all applicants — the program invites or pre-selects participants.
documents.additionalReferences: General Track announcement: https://filecoin.io/blog/posts/announcing-filecoin-propgf-batch-2-general-track/

documents.title: Filecoin ProPGF Batch 1
documents.description:
**Concluded.** Filecoin ProPGF Batch 1 was the first round of the Filecoin ProPGF program — milestone-based funding for teams building foundational infrastructure, developer tooling and essential services for the Filecoin ecosystem.

**$3.68M awarded, not budgeted.** The figure this program is usually described by is the amount AWARDED, and this record says so: the results post reads "A total of $3.68M in funding has been allocated to 14 teams" over a pull-out stat of "$3,681,800 allocated", and a later Foundation post restates it as "In ProPGF Batch 1, $3.68M was awarded across 14 teams, chosen from 38 applications." Every published phrasing is retrospective. No Batch 1 pool was ever pre-announced — unlike the Batch 2 General Track, whose $4M ceiling was announced up front — so this record carries `allocated` and deliberately no `budget`. Awards ran from $25,000 to $500,000 per project and settle in USDC, but no eligibility minimum or maximum was ever published, so no award range is recorded either.

**One figure that does not match, and why the announcement's is used.** The program's own payout ledger reports 3,741,800 for the same 14 grants — roughly $60,000 more, from post-announcement adjustments — and carries an explicit data-quality note that its Batch 1 records were entered retrospectively and in bulk rather than captured in real time. The announced total is the published one and is what this record carries; the two should not be mixed.
documents.summary: The first round of Filecoin's ProPGF public-goods program: $3,681,800 awarded to 14 teams building Filecoin infrastructure, developer tooling and essential services, paid against milestones. The round is closed and its results are published.
